A strong person should lick fresh butter mixed with sugar and honey; one suffering from consumption who subsists on milk will attain nourishment and incomparable intelligence.
Crushed crab mixed with milk, when drunk, cures consumption and fever; likewise, *bhallātaka*, *viḍaṅga*, alkali of barley, and rock salt [have similar effects].
Realgar and conch-shell powder, likewise cooked in oil, certainly cause the hair to fall out; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Having taken the juice of the mālūra fruit, one should grind a leech in it; by smearing the hands with this, there is an excellent suppression of fire.
Having taken the juice of the Śālmalī tree and placed it in donkey urine, one should scatter it at the beginning of the fire; by this means, the suppression of fire is most excellent.

Taking the belly of a female dove together with the fat of a frog, one should have a pill made from it; then the wise man should cast it into the fire. By this application, there is indeed the supreme suppression of fire.
Having chewed muṇḍī bark, vacā, musta, marica, and likewise tagara, one should immediately lick fire with the tongue.
Having powdered *gorocanā* and *bhṛṅgarāja* in equal parts with clarified butter, there will indeed be the stopping of divine waters by means of this mantra: *Oṃ agnistambhanaṃ kuru kuru*.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One! Paralyze the water! Saṃ saṃ saṃ! Ke-ka ke-kaḥ! Caracara! This is the mantra for paralyzing water; O Śiva, it paralyzes the water.
If one buries a vulture bone, a cow bone, or likewise a discarded flower offering at the door of an enemy, that person shall meet his death.
One should apply five red flowers of distinct species, combined with saffron and endowed with one's own blood.
O Rudra, by grinding one pala of gorocanā together with the flower, this tilaka applied by a woman or a man is a means of subjugation.
Brahmadaṇḍī under the Puṣya asterism, when consumed with food or drink, is a means of subjugation; one should drink warm water boiled with one pala of Yaṣṭimadhu.
O Maheśvara, this mantra—*oṃ hrūṃ jaḥ*—indeed removes constipation and heart-pain; O Rudra, it destroys all poison produced by scorpions.
Long pepper, fresh butter, ginger, rock salt, black pepper, curd, and costus—these, used as a nasal drop or taken by mouth, will remove poison.
O Śiva, by drinking and applying as an ointment this mixture of triphalā, fresh ginger, kuṣṭha, and sandalwood combined with ghee, the destruction of poison shall occur.
The eyes of a pigeon, yellow orpiment, and realgar—by the application of these, one destroys poison just as Vainateya destroys serpents.
O Bull-bannered Lord, this application of rock salt and the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), combined with curd, honey, and clarified butter, destroys the poison of a scorpion.
O Rudra, having boiled *brahmadaṇḍī* and sesame seeds, one should drink the powder of the three pungents (*trikaṭuka*); this will destroy abdominal tumors (*gulma*) and even obstructed blood.

Having drunk milk mixed with honey, one should stop the flow of blood; one should also smear the vulva and the navel with the root of *āṭarūpaka*. A woman will give birth easily; there is no need for doubt in this matter.
O Bull-bannered One, by drinking sugar mixed with honey along with rice-water, there occurs the pacification of bloody diarrhea.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-second chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa. Hari said: O Lord whose crest is marked by the crescent moon, by drinking [a decoction of] black pepper, ginger, and the bark of the *kuṭaja* tree, *grahaṇī* (chronic diarrhea) shall be destroyed.
One should grind long pepper, the root of long pepper, black pepper, tagara, vacā, the resin of devadāru, and pāṭhā together with milk.
By this very application, dysentery is indeed destroyed; an ointment made from long pepper and sesame flowers removes jaundice.
Harītakī combined with an equal amount of jaggery and mixed with honey, O Rudra, acts as a purgative; of this there is no doubt.
Triphalā, citraka, citra, and likewise kaṭukarohiṇī—this is indeed an excellent purgative that removes ūrustambha (stiffness of the thighs).
One should boil harītakī, śṛṅgavera, devadāru, and candana with goat’s milk, along with the root of apāmārga; or by using jayantī, one shall destroy ūrustambha within seven nights.

One should have an infinite quantity of ginger made into a fine powder; by using pills composed of this powder and guggulu in equal parts with jaggery, one destroys wind disorders, diseases located in the tendons, and sluggish digestive fire.
Having uprooted the saṅkhapuṣpī plant together with its flowers, leaves, and roots, one should drink it with goat's milk to remove epilepsy.
One should drink aśvagandhā and abhayā together with water; blood-bile (raktapitta) will be destroyed—there is no need for hesitation in this matter.
Having made a powder of *harītakī* and *kuṣṭha*, one should fill the mouth with it; then, by drinking cold water, all vomiting is prevented.
Guḍūcī, padmaka, āriṣṭa, dhānyaka, and red sandalwood destroy fever caused by pitta and kapha, vomiting, burning sensations, and thirst, and they kindle the digestive fire. Oṃ huṃ namaḥ.
Having tied *śaṅkhapuṣpī* to the ears, one shall indeed remove fever with this mantra: *oṃ jambhinī stambhinī mohaya sarvavyādhīn me vajreṇa ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ sarvavyādhīn me vajreṇa phaṭ*.
Having recited the mantra over eight hundred flowers and placed them in one's hand, one should touch the fingernail; O Rudra, this cures quartan fever as well as other types of fever.
Jambū fruit, turmeric, and the slough of a snake—this incense cures all fevers and also removes quartan fever.
One should cook oil with *karavīra*, *bhṛṅgapattra*, salt, *kuṣṭha*, and *karkaṭa* along with four times the amount of urine; when massaged, it indeed removes scabies, eczema, leprosy, and ulcers.
O Rudra, spleen disease is destroyed by drinking long pepper with honey, as well as by eating sweet foods and by the consumption of surana.
One should insert long pepper and turmeric combined with cow's urine into the anal opening, which will eliminate hemorrhoids.
Goat’s milk and ginger, when drunk together, destroy diseases such as splenic enlargement (plīha). Likewise, rock salt, viḍaṅga, somarājī, and mustard seeds [are effective].
One should grind the two types of *rajanī* (turmeric) and *viṣa* (aconite) with cow’s urine; by applying that as an ointment with *nimba* leaves and so forth, leprosy (*kuṣṭha*) is destroyed.
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-third chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

Hari said: An application of a paste made from *rajanī* (turmeric), *kadalī* (plantain), and *kṣāra* (alkali) destroys *sidhma* (vitiligo). Furthermore, by grinding one part of *kuṣṭha* and two parts of *pathyā* (harītakī) with warm water, it destroys pain in the waist.
Haritaki, fresh butter, sugar, and long pepper, when combined, remove jaundice through drinking; there is no need for hesitation in this matter.
One should cook ghee with the leaf of the *āṭarūṣaka* over a gentle fire; having then made it into a powder, this ointment is supreme for removing the disease of hemorrhoids (*arśas*).
By drinking guggulu combined with the three myrobalans (triphalā), fistula-in-ano (bhagandara) is destroyed; one should likewise cook ajājī and śṛṅgavera with the scum (maṇḍa) of boiled rice.
Yavakṣāra combined with salt destroys dysuria; likewise, sugar and yavakṣāra bring about the destruction of dysuria.

The fire from a funeral pyre, the excrement of a wagtail, the froth of a horse, *saubhāñjana*, and *vāsanetra*—when a man is fumigated with these, O Śiva, he becomes invisible even to all the gods, let alone to human beings.
Having burned sesame seeds and barley, one should make them into a soot and apply it; by that very oil mixed with the soot, one who has been burned by fire will become well.

An ointment made from the *lajjālū* plant (*śarapuṅkhā*) mixed with clarified butter destroys fire. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One! Ṭha Ṭha! Cut, cut! Destroy, destroy the blazing, flaming fire! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
The root of *nirguṇḍī* tied to the hand quickly removes fever; likewise, having cut the root of white *guñjā* into seven pieces [and tying it], [the same result follows].
By tying [this] in the hand, one destroys hemorrhoids without a doubt; with Viṣṇukrāntā and goat’s urine, there is protection against thieves, tigers, and the like.
One should perform all rites using the roots of *brahmadaṇḍī*; indeed, the powder of *triphalā* taken with clarified butter destroys skin diseases (*kuṣṭha*).
Clarified butter prepared with *punarnavā*, *bilva*, and *pippalī*, when drunk, removes hoarseness, asthma, and cough, and for women, it promotes conception.
Or one may eat the seed of the *narī* plant cooked with milk and clarified butter; when combined with ghee and sugar, from that one's semen shall become inexhaustible.
Viḍaṅga, madhuka, pāṭhā, māṃsī, sarjarasa, as well as rāsnā, triphalā, apāmārga, and manaḥśilā.
One should grind *udumbara* and *dhātakī* with sesame oil and smear it upon the vulva and the penis; thus, the man and woman will be mutually fond of one another.
"Salutations to you, O Lord, the Giver of Boons! O Attractor, O Attractress, O Enchanting One, Svāhā! Then, with oil from the yoni-linga, O Śaṅkara, [one should perform] the marking.
Punarnavā, amṛtā, dūrvā, kanaka, and aindravāruṇī—their juices should be rubbed together with the juice of jātī seeds.
Having placed the mercury in the middle of the crucible, its killing (māraṇa) is thus described; milk combined with honey and clarified butter destroys wrinkles and graying hair.
Honey, clarified butter, jaggery, copper, and the juice of *kāravella*—from heating these, silver is produced; now listen to the method for making gold.
One should wear yellow *dhātrī* flowers and one *pala* of lead; and from the branch of *lāṅgalikā*, gold shall arise from fire.
By lighting a lamp with oil from dhattūra seeds, one who is seated in meditative absorption will not be seen even by one stationed in the sky.
Just as a frog is naturally drawn to a clay bull, so too one who possesses the limbs of Śaṅkara sniffs the incense and bellows; he even displays wonder like a bull—of this there is no doubt.
And at night, with mustard oil and the insect known as a firefly, a lamp lit from those two blazes like a mass of flames from the mouth of Agni.

O Rudra, having burned the powder of a muskrat, one should apply it as an ointment; if one applies it correctly, the victim is instantly consumed by fire. Liberation occurs through sandalwood; by drinking it or applying it as an ointment, one becomes happy.
If one personally applies collyrium made from the ichor of an elephant to one's eyes, one will be victorious in battle and become a great hero.
Having indeed grasped the fang of a water-snake, one should cast it into the mouth; then, while remaining within the water, one stands without wavering, just as if on dry land.
One should combine the eyes and fangs of a crocodile, as well as bones and blood, together with fat and oil in one place; having smeared oneself with that, one should remain in water for three days.

The eyes of a crocodile, the heart of a tortoise, the fat and bones of a mouse, and likewise the fat of a porpoise—by applying these together as an ointment, one may remain in water as if in one's own home.
Iron powder drunk with buttermilk becomes a remover of jaundice; likewise, the root of *taṇḍulīyaka* and *gokṣūra* drunk with milk [has the same effect].
The root of the *jātī* plant taken with buttermilk removes diseases of the mouth; likewise, the root of the *kola* plant, when drunk with buttermilk, cures indigestion.
Satakra, kuśamala, or even the root of markaṭī, or the root of vākucī with sour gruel (kāñjika), indeed cures dental diseases.
Likewise, O Śiva, drinking the root of indravāruṇī with water removes poison and the like; or, by consuming the root of surabhikā, that [poison] shall be destroyed.
Powdered *guñjā* mixed with sour gruel (*kāñjika*), when applied as a paste, removes diseases of the head; likewise do *balā*, *atibalā*, *yaṣṭīmadhu*, sugar, and honey combined together.
When drunk, it causes a barren woman to conceive; there is no need for deliberation on this point. [Likewise,] the root of white Aparājitā combined with Pippalī and Śuṇṭhikā [is effective].
When ground into a paste and applied as a head-ointment, it destroys headache; by drinking the top shoots of *nirguṇḍikā*, one shall destroy *gaṇḍamālā*.
One should consume the alkali derived from *ketakī* leaves together with jaggery; or, by drinking *śarapuṅkhā* with buttermilk, one shall destroy splenic enlargement.

The resin of the *mātuluṅga* tree, combined with jaggery and clarified butter, certainly destroys pains born of wind and bile when used as a drink. Likewise, ginger, black salt, and asafoetida, when drunk, remove diseases of the heart.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-fourth chapter in the section on medical science within the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa 185. Hari said: "Āṃ Gaṇapataye"—this mantra of Gaṇapati bestows wealth and knowledge.

Having recited this eight-thousand-verse [text] and then tied it around one's topknot, one will achieve victory in legal disputes; moreover, by reciting it a hundred times, one becomes beloved by people.
O Rudra, one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of black sesame seeds smeared with ghee; within three days, the king will become submissive.

Having fasted on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days and having worshipped Vighnarāja (Gaṇeśa), one should offer one thousand and eight oblations of sesame seeds and unbroken rice grains; he shall become unconquerable in battle, and all shall serve him.
Having recited it eight thousand times, and then indeed eight hundred times, one should bind the topknot; thus victory shall be attained in the royal court and in legal proceedings.
Any man who, at the time of dawn, places the syllable *hrīṃ* together with the *visarga* on the foreheads of women, certainly brings them under his control.
Having placed [the mantra] in the abode of a woman with a well-concentrated mind, one should make that passionate woman full of longing; there is no need for deliberation in this matter.
Whoever, being pure and with a disciplined mind, performs ten thousand oblations, women will always come under his control at the mere sight of him.
When a tilaka is made with realgar, patraka, gorocana, and saffron, women come under one's control.
Having made a tilaka with bhr̥ṅgarāja, sahadevā, vacā, and white aparājitā, one shall bring the three worlds under one's control.

A man who makes a tilaka mark with a wick prepared from both gorocanā and the bile of a fish, using his left little finger, brings the entire three worlds under his control; of this there is no doubt.

O Mahādeva, *gorocanā* is infused with the blood of the *dhātu*. Having prepared a tilaka with these, whatever man she gazes upon, she shall bring him under her control at that very moment; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Nāgeśvara, śaileya, tvak, patra, and harītakī, combined with candana, kuṣṭha, sūkṣmailā, and red śāli rice.
O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, beloved of Pārvatī, this incense, which acts as a subduer through the arrows of Smara, destroys the afflictions of love during the time of dalliance.
A man who, having taken his own semen with his left hand, smears it upon the left foot of a passionate woman, shall become dear to her.
O Mahādeva, by smearing the linga with rock salt, pigeon dung, and honey, one will indeed become the subduer of women.

Having taken any five red flowers whatsoever, one should grind them together with an equal amount of *priyaṅgu* in a single mixture; by smearing this upon the *liṅga*, a woman will come under one's control.
Hayagandhā, mañjiṣṭhā, mālatī flowers, and white mustard—by smearing a liṅga with these, one becomes dear to women.

The root of *kākajaṅghā*, when drunk with milk, cures emaciation. For those who consume *aśvagandhā*, *nāgabalā*, jaggery, and black gram, their appearance becomes like that of those moving in the prime of youth.
O Rudra, either iron powder combined with the powder of the three myrobalans (triphalā), or the powder of the three myrobalans alone, when consumed with honey, cures the colic known as pariṇāma-śūla.

O Śiva, drinking boiled water mixed with the ash of a snail shell, as well as deer horn burnt by fire combined with cow's clarified butter, shall bring about the destruction of pains in the heart and the back.
Asafoetida, black salt, ginger, and the great medicine (mustard) of Śiva—water boiled with these, when drunk, indeed cures all types of colic.
The root of Apāmārga combined with sea salt, when tasted, acts as a remedy for colic caused by indigestion.
O Rudra, O Śaṅkara, the sprout of a banyan tree rubbed with rice-water and drunk with *takra* brings diarrhea to an end.
Half a karṣa of aṅkoṭa root ground with rice-water, when drunk, O Lord of Beings, removes all types of diarrhea and dysentery.
Powdered long pepper, dry ginger, and *kuṭaja* bark, combined with jaggery and drunk in gradually doubling doses, destroys the disease of *grahaṇī*.
O Śiva, a pill made from the root of white Aparājitā, turmeric, beeswax, rice, Apāmārga, and Trikaṭu certainly destroys the great disease of cholera; of this there is no doubt.
O Śaṅkara, the powder of each of these—triphalā, aguru, bhūteśa, śilājatu, and harītakī—when mixed with honey and drunk, brings all types of urinary disorders (meha) to an end.
One *prastha* of *arka* milk and the same amount of sesame oil, along with one *pala* each of realgar, black pepper, and vermilion.
Having made it into a powder, one should then dry it in a copper vessel using sunlight; when drunk with the milk of Snuhī and rock salt (saindhava), it will alleviate colic.
The three pungents, the three myrobalans, and black sesame oil at night, as well as realgar, neem leaves, jasmine flowers, and goat’s milk.
Then, one should grind that urine with conch-shell and sandalwood; having made a wick from these, one should then apply it as an ointment to the eyes.
The film, cataract, ophthalmia, and darkness of vision are destroyed; indeed, the powder of *vibhītaka* with honey is a destroyer of asthma.
The powder of pippalī and triphalā, combined with honey and rock salt, cures all diseases, fever, asthma, consumption, chronic catarrh, and heart ailments.

One should indeed saturate the powder of *devadāru* twenty-one times with goat’s urine; one should then apply it as an ointment to the eyes. By this, night-blindness, cataracts, and even the absence of eyelashes shall be destroyed.
O Rudra, by applying an ointment made of pippalī, ketakī, haridrā, āmalaka, and vacā mixed with milk, all eye diseases shall be destroyed.
O Śiva, O Hara, if the roots of *kākajaṅghā* and *śigru* are held in the mouth after chewing them, there will indeed be the destruction of dental worms.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-sixth chapter, titled "The Application of Mantras, Tantras, and Medicine," in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa within the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Hari said: The essence of *guḍūcī* drunk with honey cures urinary disorders (*prameha*). Likewise, the root of *gohālikā* drunk combined with sesame, curd, and clarified butter [is effective].
O Śaṅkara, boiled *niruddhamūtra* cures [the disease]; likewise, when drunk together with *sauvarcala* salt, it indeed removes hiccups.
O Rudra, the root of *gorakṣakarkaṭī* ground with cold water and drunk for only three days will destroy urinary gravel.
Having ground the root of *mālatī* and prepared it with goat’s milk during the summer season, one who takes it along with sugar will remove urinary obstruction and indeed cure jaundice and gravel.
The root of the *dvijayaṣṭi* plant ground with rice-water, when applied as a paste, removes *gaṇḍamālā* and even the incurable *galagaṇḍa*.
By smearing it with the powder of *rasāñjana* and *harītakī*, a person shall destroy diseases; there is no need for hesitation in this matter.
O Rudra, by the application of a paste made from the root of *karavīra* and a paste of *pūgaphala*, the disease of men is destroyed; now I shall tell you another method.

By applying a paste of *dantī* root, *haridrā*, and *citraka*, hemorrhoids (*bhagaṇdara*) shall be destroyed; I shall now describe another formulation: O Lord of Umā, for hemorrhoids from which blood has been sucked out by leeches, [this is the remedy].
If the bone of a cat is rubbed with water from the three myrobalans (triphalā) and applied as an ointment, then blood will not flow; there is no need for hesitation in this matter.

Haridrā, processed many times with the milky sap of Snuhī, forms a pill that destroys hemorrhoids when applied as an ointment, O Bull-bannered Lord; likewise, Ghoṣā fruit and rock salt, ground together, are a supreme remedy for hemorrhoids.
O Śiva, cow’s clarified butter prepared with three times the amount of palāśa-alkali water and mixed with the three pungents (trikaṭu), when drunk, destroys hemorrhoids.
The burnt fruit of the *bilva* tree destroys hemorrhoids caused by blood; likewise, one may eat black sesame seeds combined with fresh butter.
O Bull-bannered One, powdered ginger mixed with alkali of barley and an equal amount of jaggery certainly increases the digestive fire when taken at dawn.
Water boiled with ginger, when drunk, indeed stimulates the digestive fire; likewise, O Rudra, *harītakī*, rock salt, *citraka*, and long pepper [do so].
Their powder, when drunk with warm water, produces extreme hunger; likewise, the meat of a pig, when drunk along with clarified butter, produces extreme hunger.
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-sixth chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—187—Hari said: "What are the leaves of the Hastikarṇapalāśa?"
O Hara, O Śiva, one hundred palas of this powder, which liberates one from all diseases, should be ground into a fine powder.
O Bull-bannered One, O Rudra, if one consumes it with milk for seven days, it makes a man a possessor of the Vedas, with the gait and prowess of a lion-king.
O Rudra, by constantly consuming milk, one becomes sixteen years of age, possesses a lifespan of a thousand years, and has a complexion resembling a ruby.
Milk combined with honey and clarified butter bestows longevity; when consumed together with honey, it grants a lifespan of ten thousand years.
It makes a man a retainer of the Vedas and beloved by women; when eaten daily with curd, it renders the body like adamant.
A man who has consumed that [substance], combined with a row of filaments and mixed with sour gruel (kāñjika), shall live for a thousand years.
Honey processed with the three myrobalans (triphalā) indeed bestows a divine body for a hundred years, free from wrinkles and grey hair, and grants keen vision.
By consuming this powder mixed with clarified butter, even a blind man may see; moreover, an application of it combined with buffalo milk produces black hair.
O Bull-bannered One, even for one who is bald, hair grows back by means of this powder mixed with oil; it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
By merely rubbing that [ointment] on, one is liberated from all passion; by applying it as an eye-salve for a month with the powder of goat's milk, one gains divine vision.
Having taken the seeds of the *palāśa* tree in the month of Śrāvaṇa and freed them from their husks, one should consume their powder with fresh butter.

Having bowed to Lord Hari, one should daily consume half a *karṣa* of the sixty kinds of ancient grains while drinking wholesome water; O Hara, such a person shall live for thousands of years, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Having collected the root of Bhṛṅgarāja under the Puṣya asterism, one should prepare its powder and consume it with Sauvīra.

By practicing this for only one month, a man becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair; he shall live for five hundred years and possess the strength of an elephant. O Rudra, by consuming it under the Puṣya asterism, he will become one who retains whatever he hears.
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-seventh chapter, titled "The Life-Prolonging Yoga," in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the *Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa*.

Hari said: A wound shall become free of pus and healed when filled with clarified butter (*ghṛta*). By rubbing the root of the *apāmārga* plant with both hands, its juice prevents the flow of blood from a wound when applied as a filling.

O Rudra, the root of lāṅgalikā and likewise that of ikṣudarbha—when the opening of the wound is smeared with these, the foreign object (śalya) emerges from the wound, O Śaṅkara, even if it has been lodged there for a long time, by way of that path.
The root of *bālamūla* or the root of *meṣaśṛṅgī*, ground with water and applied as an ointment, heals a chronic wound or sinus tract that has been present for a long time.
The consumption of *kodrava* grain with buffalo meat, combined with the powder of *hiṅgu* root, removes sinus ulcers (*nāḍī-vraṇa*).
The fruit of the *brahmayaṣṭi* ground with water and smeared [on the body], or rubbed [on it] with that same [mixture], destroys blood disorders; of this there is no doubt.
Barley ash, viḍaṅga, and indeed sulphur, along with ginger—the powder of these should be mixed with blood.
O Śiva, that which is smeared with the [excrement] of a lizard destroys an abscess; likewise, the seeds of *saubhāñjana* together with linseed and black ink [achieve the same].
O Śaṅkara, all these, including yellow mustard seeds, ground with non-sour buttermilk, will indeed destroy glandular swellings (granthika).
The root of white Aparājitā ground with rice-water; by administering it as a nasal drop (nasya), there shall be the dispersal of a multitude of spirits.

An inhalation of Agasti flowers together with long pepper (marica) indeed removes colic. O Śiva, an ointment made from snake-skin, asafoetida (hiṅgu), neem leaves, barley, and white mustard seeds removes possession by malevolent spirits (bhūta).
O Śiva, an ointment prepared from these—gorocanā, marīca, pippalī, saindhava, and honey—shall be a remover of planetary influences and malevolent spirits.
Incense made from guggulu and an owl's tail will ward off the seizing spirits (grahas); one who is afflicted by quartan fevers shall be liberated, provided they are veiled in black cloth.
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-eighth chapter, titled "The Treatment of Wounds," in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa within the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—189.
Hari said: By filling the eyes with the juice of the flowers of white Aparājitā, the film (paṭala) is destroyed; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter.
O blue-and-red one, crusher of gods and demons, by chewing the root of *gokṣuraka* itself, the pain of dental caries shall be destroyed.
If a woman, having fasted, drinks the root of white arka with cow's milk on the first day of her menstrual period, it cures her abdominal tumors and colic.

A woman who has become pure through her menstrual period, having fastened a white *arka* flower—taken according to the prescribed rite and previously consecrated with mantras—around her waist, will give birth.
Take a root of either the *palāśa* or the *apāmārga* held in the hand; it removes all fevers and drives away spirits, ghosts, and the like.
O Supreme Lord, the root of the scorpion-plant (vṛścikamūla), drunk in the morning with water that has stood overnight, shall destroy burning fever.
When tied upon the crest-lock (śikhā), it shall destroy the fevers lasting for one day; when drunk with water that has stood overnight, it shall remove all poisons.
Whether it be a man or a woman, whoever offers the root of the *lajjālukā* plant together with their own semen shall undoubtedly enter into enmity.
Whoever grinds the root of pāṭhā with cow’s ghee and drinks it, all poison shall be destroyed; there is no need for hesitation in this matter.

Just as with the root of the *śirīṣa* tree soaked in water that has stood overnight, by filling the ears with the juice of the root of red *citraka*, the disease of jaundice (*kāmalā*) will be destroyed; of this there is no doubt.
The root of white *kokilākṣa*, combined with goat’s milk and drunk for three weeks, will surely bring about the destruction of consumption disease (*kṣayaroga*).
One should drink the flower of the coconut combined with goat's milk; by this, his three types of *raktavāta* (blood-wind disorder) are destroyed.

One should prepare a garland well-arranged from the roots of the *sudarśana* plant; when tied around the neck, it destroys the afflictions caused by the *grahas*, *bhūtas*, and those that manifest every third day (*tryāhika*).
O Rudra, the flower and the root of the white guñjā plant, when taken and placed in the mouth, shall remove many kinds of diverse poisons.

Bound upon the hand, it wards off arrows; bound upon the neck, it removes the influence of malevolent planets and the like. Bound upon the waist on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, O Nīlalohita, it shall take away the fear of lions and other wild beasts.
O Lord, one should wear the root of *viṣṇukrāntā* tied to the ear with a silk thread; O Lord of Beings, there will certainly be no fear of crocodiles and other such dangers.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-ninth chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa. Hari said: The root of Aparājitā combined with cow’s urine, when drunk, quickly removes Gaṇḍamālā; of this there is no doubt.

Furthermore, O Lord, the root of *indravāruṇī* drunk according to the prescribed rite, along with *jiṅginī*, castor root, and *śūkaśimbī*, O Rudra, when administered with cold water, removes pain in the arms and neck.
Buffalo butter, *aśvagandhā*, long pepper (*pippalī*), *vacā*, and the two types of *kuṣṭha*—this ointment removes pain from the penis, the channels, and the breasts.
A paste made from the powder of Kuṣṭha and Nāgabalā combined with fresh butter, when applied, will make the thighs and buttocks of young women beautiful and well-rounded.
If the root of *indravāruṇikā* is uprooted and cast from a great distance under someone's name, that person’s spleen disease will perish.
The root of white punarnavā, when drunk with rice-water, destroys abscesses; there is no need for hesitation in this matter.
The alkali of plantain leaves prepared with water—by consuming it, all diseases of the abdomen are destroyed.
Having taken the root of the plantain tree combined with jaggery and clarified butter, and having prepared it over a fire, its consumption will remove the worms residing within the stomach.
If one regularly consumes the powder of neem leaves and āmalaka at dawn, his leprosy will be destroyed.
Harītakī, viḍaṅga, turmeric, white mustard seeds, the roots of somarāja and karañja, and raudhava—these, when ground with cow’s urine, are indeed destroyers of the disease of leprosy (kuṣṭha).
One part of triphalā and two parts of śivā (harītakī), along with the seeds of somarāja, when eaten with pathyā (harītakī), cure ringworm.
A decoction of *amlātaka* with cow’s urine, combined with salt and rubbed in a bronze vessel until it becomes coarse, destroys *kuṣṭha* and *dadru* when applied as an ointment.
Turmeric, yellow orpiment, dūrvā grass, cow’s urine, and rock salt—this ointment destroys ringworm, scabies, and likewise artificial poison.

O Rudra, the seeds of Soma-rāja mixed with fresh butter and tasted with honey indeed remove white leprosy; there is no need for hesitation regarding this when accompanied by food and drink prepared with buttermilk.
O Rudra, a paste made from the root of white Aparājitā ground with water and applied for one month destroys white leprosy.
O Bull-bannered Lord, scabies and the disease called *durnāmā* (ringworm) are destroyed by the application of buffalo butter and vermilion mixed with black pepper.
O Lord, the dried root of gambhārī, cooked and combined with milk, when consumed, brings about the destruction of śuklapitta.
O Rudra, by rubbing the seeds of radish with the juice of apāmārga and applying that paste, sidhmaka is destroyed.

Turmeric combined with the juice of plantain and sugarcane removes *sidhma*. O Mahādeva, by massaging with the alkali of plantain and *apāmārga* mixed with castor oil, *sidhma* is destroyed instantly.
Kūṣmāṇḍa, nāla, and alkali, along with cow’s urine in accordance with reality, and turmeric ground with water, should be cooked over a gentle fire.
O Bull-bannered Lord, one should prepare a body rub for her with buffalo dung, O Ishvara, which will bring about the perfection of her limbs.
A man whose body has been rubbed with a mixture of sesame, mustard, the two types of turmeric, and kuṣṭha will be fragrant instead of foul-smelling.
Manohara, by daily applying a paste of dūrvā grass, kākajaṅghā, the flowers of arjuna combined with jambū leaves, and lodhra, removes the foul odor of the body.
A powder made from *lodhra* flowers and gold dust is appropriate; for one whose body has been rubbed with this, the affliction of the summer heat shall not prevail.
Sprinkling with milk at dawn destroys the affliction caused by heat; moreover, an ointment made from *kākajaṅghā* serves as a cosmetic for the body.
Licorice, sugar, the juice of vāsaka, and honey—this, when drunk, cures blood-bile (raktapitta), jaundice (kāmalā), and anemia (pāṇḍuroga).
The juice of vāsaka drunk with honey removes *raktapitta*; when drunk with water at the time of dawn, it removes even severe catarrh (*pīnasa*).
O Maheśvara, the powder of *bibhītaka*, *pippalī*, and rock salt, when drunk with *kāñjika* vinegar, destroys hoarseness of voice.
One should consume a powder of *āmalaka* mixed with cow's milk; likewise, realgar, the root of *balā*, *kola-panasa*, and *guggulu*.
O Maheśvara, a wick made from these—namely, *jātipatra*, *kolapatra*, and realgar—and burned in a fire of *badarī* wood, when used for smoking, removes cough; of this there is no doubt.
The powder of triphalā and pippalī, consumed with honey at the beginning of a meal, quickly removes thirst when taken together with honey.

Water boiled with the root of the *bilva* tree, honey, and *guḍūcī*, when drunk, removes the three types of vomiting; of this there is no doubt. *Dūrvā* grass ground with rice-water, when drunk, is a cure for vomiting.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninetieth chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Hari said: The root of Punarnavā, white in color, gathered under the Puṣya asterism—when its juice is drunk, serpents do not remain in one's dwellings.
O Bull-bannered One, he who indeed wears an image of Tārkṣya fashioned from the teeth of a bear shall not be seen by serpents for as long as he lives.
O Rudra, those who drink the root of the *śalmali* tree with water under the asterism of Puṣya will have serpents whose fangs are destroyed; of this there is no doubt.

Under the asterism Puṣya, one should catch snakes by tying the root of the *lajjālukā* plant to the hand; or else, one may seize them by means of an ointment—there is no need for hesitation in this matter.

The root of the white *arka* tree, gathered under the asterism Puṣya, when drunk with cold water, destroys the venom of biting insects as well as poison derived from the *karavīra* and other such sources.
The root of mahākāla ground with kāñjika indeed destroys the poison of voḍra and ḍuṇḍubha snakes when applied as a plaster.
The root of *taṇḍulīyaka* ground with rice-water and drunk together with clarified butter removes all poisons.
The root of the blue water-moss (nīlī-lajjālukā), ground with rice-water and drunk, will destroy the poison of that stinging insect for either one or both.
The fresh juice of the kūṣmāṇḍaka fruit, when drunk together with jaggery, sugar, and milk, indeed destroys the poison of a stinging insect.
Likewise, sugar mixed with liquorice (yaṣṭīmadhu) and consumed together with the root of kodrava and with *moha* (delusion) acts as a remover of [fever].
And by drinking goat's milk for three nights, one may remove the poison of mice; likewise, by drinking three mouthfuls of cool water.
For one whose mouth has been scorched by betel, the flow of saliva ceases; by drinking ghee with sugar, the intoxication from drinking liquor is indeed removed.
O Maheśvara, water well-boiled with the root of black aṅkola, when drunk, destroys the poison of *gara* within three nights.
O Mahādeva, warm cow’s ghee combined with rock salt shall destroy the pain arising from a scorpion sting.
Kusumbha, saffron, yellow orpiment, realgar, karañja, and meat, as well as the root of the arka plant, O Śaṅkara.

O Śiva, by eating these, the poison of men shall be destroyed; and by the offering of lamp oil, O Śiva, the poison born of the bites of insects and the *kharjūraka* shall surely perish—of this there is no doubt.
The poison of a scorpion at the site of the sting is destroyed by ginger combined with *tagara*, and the poison of honey-bees is destroyed by an ointment made from these [same ingredients].
One should apply a plaster of *śatapuṣpā* and rock salt with clarified butter; or else, one should rub the seeds of *śirīṣa* that have been prepared with milk.
O Mahādeva, by anointing with that [ointment], the poison born of a dog is destroyed; likewise, the poison born of a frog is destroyed by sprinkling water upon a blazing fire.
O Lord whose crest is marked by the moon, by drinking milk and other substances mixed with dhattūra and garlic along with jaggery, the poison of those who are swollen shall be destroyed.
Water boiled with the bark of the *vaṭa*, *nimba*, and *śamī* trees—by sprinkling that, the poisonous pain of the mouth and teeth shall indeed be destroyed.

O Lord of Umā, by anointing with devadāru, by anointing with red ochre (gairika), and likewise by anointing with nāgeśvara, daridra, mañjiṣṭhaka, and hara, the poison of spiders is destroyed through these ointments.
The seeds of the karañja tree, the leaves of the varuṇa tree, sesame, and mustard seeds indeed destroy poison; there is no doubt about this.
O Hara, if ghee and *kumārī* leaves mixed with salt are administered, the itching of horses' bodies will be destroyed within ten days.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-first chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
The Glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Chapter 192. Hari said: Take eight parts of Citraka, sixteen parts of Śūraṇa, four parts of Śuṇṭhī, and likewise two parts of Marica.

Take three parts of long pepper root (pippalīmūla), four parts of embelia (viḍaṅga), eight parts of musalī, and four parts of the three myrobalans (triphalā). One should prepare boluses (modaka) from these with double the amount of jaggery (guḍa).
Indeed, its consumption cures indigestion, anemia, jaundice, dysentery, weak digestion, and even splenic enlargement.
Bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā, pāribhadraka, prasāraṇī, aśvagandhā, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārikā.
Balā, atibalā, rāsnā, śvadaṃṣṭrā, punarnavā, eraṇḍa, śārivā, parṇa, guḍūcī, and kapikacchukā.
One should boil ten palas of these [drugs] in pure water; with that decoction reduced to one-fourth, one should cook it in a vessel of oil.
Having given either goat's milk or cow's milk four times the quantity [of the oil], one should cause śatāvarī and rock salt to be added in an amount equal to the oil.
I shall now describe those substances which are to be ground; listen to that. They are: śatapuṣpā, devadāru, balā, parṇa, vacā, and aguru.
One pala each of kuṣṭha, māṃsī, saindhava, and punarnavā—this oil should be administered for drinking, as nasal drops (nasya), and likewise for massage.
It destroys heartache, pain in the flanks, and scrofula; it cures epilepsy and gout, and the man becomes endowed with a beautiful body.

O Hara, even a mule would conceive a fetus [by this], how much more so a human woman? This oil should be administered to horses broken by wind, as well as to elephants and humans, for all those afflicted with disorders of the wind (vāta).
Sesame oil prepared with asafoetida, tumburu, and ginger is indeed the best for filling the ear; it is supreme for removing earache.
One should take the alkali of dried radish and ginger, along with asafoetida and dry ginger; to these, one should add four times the amount of buttermilk and cook this oil.
Deafness, earache, and the discharge of pus from the ears, as well as worms, are destroyed by filling the ears with this oil.
The alkali of dried radish and ginger, realgar, dry ginger, *śatapuṣpā*, *vacā*, *kuṣṭha*, *dāruśigru*, and *rasāñjana*.
Sauvarcala salt, yavakṣāra, sea salt, and likewise rock salt; granthika, viḍa salt, and musta; honey, and four times as much fermented gruel (śukta).
The juice of mātuluṅga and the juice of kadalī as well—oil should be cooked with these; it is the supreme remedy for removing earache.
Deafness, tinnitus, and the terrible discharge of pus from the ears—these worms are destroyed by filling the ears with this oil.
O you who have the moon as your crest-jewel, this excellent alkaline oil causes immediate destruction [of impurities]; it removes the stains from the face and teeth.
Sandalwood, saffron, spikenard, camphor, clove leaves, as well as the fruits of the jasmine, kaṅkola, betel nut, and cloves.
Aguru, musk, kuṣṭha, tagara, pādikā, gorocanā, priyaṅgu, balā, and likewise nakhī.
One should prepare the oil with sarala, saptaparṇa, lac, āmalakī, and likewise padmaka.
It is the supreme remover of sweat, impurities, foul odors, itching, and skin diseases; O Rudra, one may approach a hundred women, and even a barren woman obtains a son.
Yavānī, citraka, coriander, the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), cumin, as well as sauvarcala salt, viḍa salt, long pepper root, and black mustard.
One should cook one prastha of ghee with these [drugs] combined with eight prasthas of water; this indeed cures hemorrhoids, abdominal tumors, and swelling, and truly kindles the digestive fire.
Black pepper, trivṛt, kuṣṭha, yellow orpiment, realgar, devadāru, the two types of haridrā, kuṣṭha, māṃsī, and sandalwood.
Viśālā, karavīra, the milky sap of arka, and the juice of cow dung—of these, one karṣa each should be taken, along with half a pala of poison.
One should cook one *prastha* of *saṭuka* oil with eight times its amount of cow urine in either an earthen or an iron vessel, heating it slowly over a mild fire.
Scabies, eczema, ringworm, and even boils are destroyed by this massage, and a state of softness is produced.
One should rub even extensive vitiligo with this oil; even long-standing vitiligo will be destroyed at that very moment.
Patola leaves, kaṭukā, mañjiṣṭhā, śārivā, niśā, jātī leaves, śamī leaves, nimba leaves, and madhuka—these, boiled together with ghee, [form a remedy].
O Auspicious One, by applying these as a paste, wounds that are discharging and painful become free from pain; [the herbs are] Śaṅkhapuṣpī, Vacā, Soma, Brāhmī, and Brahmasuvarcalā.
One should cook one *prastha* of ghee with equal parts (one *akṣa* each) of *abhayā*, *guḍūcī*, *āṭarūṣaka*, and *vākucī*.
One prastha of the juice of Kaṇṭakārī combined with one prastha of milk—this is known as Brāhmī-ghṛta, which is supreme for producing memory and intelligence.
By using agnimantha, vacā, vāsā, pippalī, honey, and rock salt for seven nights, one is sung of by the kinnaras as if [one were] one of them.

Apāmārga, guḍūcī, vacā, kuṣṭha, śatāvarī, śaṅkhapuṣpī, abhayā, along with ghee and viḍaṅga—these, taken in equal parts, when consumed for three days, shall make a man a bearer of eight hundred granthas.
If one consumes vacā for one month with water, milk, or clarified butter, it will make a man wise and endowed with the power of retaining what he has heard.
During an eclipse of the moon or sun, if one drinks one *pala* of vacā root mixed with milk, it will instantly endow a person with great wisdom.
Water boiled with bhūnimba, nimba, triphalā, parpaṭa, paṭolī, mustaka, and vāsaka destroys [these ailments].
Eruptions and redness [occur]; there is no need for deliberation here. Kataka fruit, conch shell, rock salt, the three acridities (tryūṣaṇa), and vacā [are the remedy].
A wick made from resinous exudate, *rasāñjana*, honey, *viḍaṅga*, and realgar destroys *kāca*, *timira*, and *paṭala* as well.
One should boil two *prasthas* of *māṣaka* with one *droṇa* of water; when reduced to one-fourth, one should cook one *prastha* of oil with it.
Having added one āḍhaka of sour gruel (kāñjika), one should cause these ground powders to be mixed: punarnavā, gokṣuraka, rock salt (saindhava), the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), and vacā.
Salt, deodar, mañjiṣṭhā, and kaṇṭakārikā—these, when used as a nasal drop or taken by mouth, certainly remove even the most severe earache.
O Maheśvara, from massage one may overcome deafness and all diseases; likewise, two palas each of rock salt, ginger, and the five-fold citraka [are effective].
Then one should cook five *prasthas* of *sauvīra* and one *prastha* of oil; this cures menorrhagia, hoarseness of voice, splenic disorders, and all wind-related ailments.
The udumbara, the vaṭa, the plakṣa, the two kinds of jambū, the arjuna, the pippalī, the kadamba, the palāśa, the lodhra, and the tinduka.
Oil prepared with a decoction of madhūka, āmra, sarja, badara, padmakeśara, śirīṣa seeds, and kataka destroys wounds—even those of long standing—when applied as an ointment.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-second chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
The Glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—193. Hari said: Onion, cumin, kuṣṭha, aśvagandhā, ajamodaka, vacā, the three pungents (trikaṭuka), and salt constitute an excellent powder.
Clarified butter processed with the juices of *brāhmī* and combined with honey, when consumed for seven days, shall produce a supreme and stainless intellect.
Siddhārthaka, vacā, hiṅgu, karañja, and devadāru; mañjiṣṭhā, triphalā, viśva, śirīṣa, and the two types of rajanī.
Priyaṅgu, nimba, and the three pungents (trikaṭu), rubbed with cow’s urine, are beneficial when used as nasal drops, as an ointment, and likewise as a rubbing powder.
It removes epilepsy, poison, insanity, consumption, misfortune, and fever; it destroys fear from malevolent spirits and brings success at royal courts.
Nimba, kuṣṭha, the two types of haridrā, śigru, mustard, as well as devadāru, paṭola, and coriander, ground together with buttermilk.
One should indeed lead the body, its limbs smeared with oil, through the process of rubbing with medicinal unguents; thus, scabies and leprosy shall perish, and itching is certainly destroyed.
Sea salt, rock salt, alkali, black mustard, common salt, and soot, along with equal parts of *trivṛt* and *sūraṇaka*, should be cooked over a gentle fire with curd, cow’s urine, and milk.

One should drink this powder, which increases strength and digestive fire, with warm water; whether the previous meal is digested or undigested, one may then eat excellent meat, rice, ghee, and so forth.

This powder relieves pain of the navel, pain of the bladder, and that which arises from abdominal tumors (gulma) and the spleen; it is a destroyer of all types of pain, an inflamer of the digestive fire, and is most beneficial for pain arising from the transformation of food (pariṇāma-śūla).
Haritaki, amalaka, grapes, long pepper, kaṇṭakārikā, karkaṭaśṛṅgī, punarnavā, and ginger, when consumed, truly destroy cough.
Abhayā, āmalaka, drākṣā, pāṭhā, and vibhītaka, when eaten together with an equal amount of sugar, will become a remover of fever.
Triphalā, jujube (badara), grapes, and long pepper (pippalī) cause purgation; likewise, harītakī taken with warm water and salt causes purgation.
Turtles, fish, horses, buffaloes, cows, jackals, monkeys, cats, peacocks, crows, boars, owls, and cocks.
O Haṃsa, one should offer their feces, urine, flesh, hair, or blood as incense for the pacification of those afflicted by fever and those who are insane.
O Lord of Umā, these species of medicinal herbs have been described; they destroy diseases just as Indra’s thunderbolt destroys a tree.
The Blessed Lord Viṣṇu is the medicine; when remembered, he brings about the cessation of disease. Whether meditated upon, worshipped, or praised, this is beyond doubt.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-third chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Hari said: I shall now declare the auspicious Vaiṣṇava armor (kavaca), which removes all diseases; by means of which protection was formerly afforded to Śambhu as he was destroying the Daityas.
Having bowed down to the Lord Īśāna, who is unborn, eternal, and free from ailment; to the divine Viṣṇu, the sovereign of all, the all-pervading and imperishable.
Having paid homage to Janārdana, I bind this amulet, which is unfailing, incomparable, all-encompassing, and the warder-off of all suffering.
May Viṣṇu protect me from the front; may Kṛṣṇa guard my back; may Hara protect my head, and Janārdana my heart.
May Hṛṣīkeśa protect my mind; may Keśava protect my tongue; may Vāsudeva protect my eyes; and may the omnipresent Saṅkarṣaṇa protect my ears.
May Pradyumna protect my sense of smell, and Aniruddha my skin; may Vanamālī protect the region of my throat, and Śrīvatsa protect my lower body.
May the Discus protect my left side, warding off the Daityas; and may the Goddess Gadā protect my right side, repelling all the Asuras.
May the mace protect my belly; may the plow protect my back. May the Śārṅga bow protect my upper body, and may Nandaka protect my shanks.
May Śaṅkha protect my heels and Padma both my feet; for the sake of accomplishing all purposes, may Garuḍa always protect me.
May Varāha protect me in the water, and Vāmana on uneven ground; may Narasiṃha protect me in the forest, and may Keśava protect me everywhere.
May the Lord Hiraṇyagarbha grant me gold; may Kapila, the teacher of Sāṃkhya, bring about the equilibrium of my bodily constituents.
May the unborn Lord, who dwells in Śvetadvīpa, lead us to Śvetadvīpa; may he, the crusher of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, destroy all our enemies.
May Viṣṇu always draw away my sin from my body; may Haṃsa, Matsya, and Kūrma protect me in every direction.
May the god Trivikrama cut away all my sins; likewise, may the god Nārāyaṇa protect my intellect.
May the remainder [of my merit] produce stainless knowledge that destroys ignorance; may Vaḍavāmukha destroy whatever impurity has been committed by me.
May the Lord Dattātreya place supreme bliss upon my head with his feet, and may he grant prosperity to me along with my sons, cattle, and kinsmen.
May Rāma destroy all my enemies with his axe; may the mighty-armed son of Daśaratha, the slayer of demons, protect me forever.
May Rāma, the delight of the Yādavas, who destroyed Pralamba, Keśin, Cāṇūra, Pūtanā, and Kaṃsa, slay my enemies with his plow; may that childhood state of Kṛṣṇa grant me all my desires.
Terrified with fear, I see a man who is black and tawny, a terrible darkness of gloom, like the Ender (Antaka) himself with a noose in his hand.
Therefore, I have gone for refuge to the lotus-eyed Acyuta; I am blessed and forever fearless, for the Blessed Lord Hari belongs to me.
Having meditated upon the god Nārāyaṇa, the destroyer of all calamities, and having donned the Vaiṣṇava armor, I wander upon the surface of the earth.
I am invincible to all beings, for I am composed of all the gods; this is through the remembrance of Viṣṇu, the god of gods, who possesses immeasurable splendor.

May there be constant success for me according to the mantra as it has been uttered: "Whoever looks at me with their eyes, and whoever I look at with my eye—may Viṣṇu bind the eyes of all those who are evil and wicked."
May the spokes of that discus which belongs to Vāsudeva indeed sever my sins and strike down those who would harm me.
Among the rākṣasas and piśācas, in wildernesses and forests, in disputes, on royal highways, at gambling matches, and in quarrels;
When crossing a river in a terrible situation, when life-threatening danger has arrived, in the event of fire, thieves, or falling [from a height], and for the warding off of all malevolent planets;
In the agitation caused by lightning, snakes, or poison, in illness, or in the peril of obstacles, one should constantly recite this mantra whenever fear arises in the body.

This mantra of the Blessed One is the supreme among mantras; it is the celebrated, secret armor that destroys all sins. It is the manifestation of his own illusory form, vast and profound as the end of an eon.

O you who are without beginning or end! O seed of the world! O Padmanābha! Homage be to you! Oṃ, svāhā to Kāla! Oṃ, svāhā to Kālapuruṣa! Oṃ, svāhā to Kṛṣṇa! Oṃ, svāhā to Kṛṣṇarūpa! Oṃ, svāhā to Caṇḍa! Oṃ, svāhā to Caṇḍarūpa! Oṃ, svāhā to Pracaṇḍa! Oṃ, svāhā to Pracaṇḍarūpa! Oṃ, svāhā to Sarva! Oṃ, svāhā to Sarvarūpa! Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the World, the Sustainer of the Three Realms! Here: viṭi siviṭi siviṭi svāhā!
Oṃ, homage to Ayokhetaya! Ye ye, command them!

For the sake of the Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Antāpasmārakas, Chardanas, and Duddharas; for those fevers occurring every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, every moment, by day, by night, at twilight, and all other such fevers; and for the poisons of spiders, insects, thorns, Pūtanās, serpents, and both stationary and moving [venoms]—make this body of mine wholesome!
*Sphuṭa sphuṭa sphuṭa prakoṭa laṣphaṭa vikaṭadaṃṣṭra*, may he protect me from the east! Oṃ hai hai!

Hai hai! You who are struck by the time of a thousand suns, victory to you! Protect me from the west! Oṃ nivi nivi! You whose form is like the blazing flame of a fire, great tawny one, protect me from the north! Oṃ vili vili mili mili! O Garuḍī, Garuḍī! May Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Viṣamohā, and Viṣamā destroy the most terrible poison!
Svāhā! Protect me from the south! Look upon me! Protect, protect me from all calamities and fears caused by spirits!

Victory, victory, O Victorious One! By that [name], the fear of enemies and the pride born of musical instruments are destroyed. May the Unfallen One (Acyuta), the dispeller of fear, grant fearlessness to those who are without fear. May they all enter his entire belly, just as the rays of light enter the setting sun after thousands of aeons have passed. May Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha—Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa, and Hari—destroy all my fevers.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Vaiṣṇava Armor," in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa within the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Chapter 195—Hari said: Listen to that Vidyā which grants all desires within seven nights: "Salutations to You, the Blessed One; we meditate upon Vāsudeva."
Salutations to Pradyumna, to Aniruddha, and to Saṅkarṣaṇa; salutations to the one who is pure consciousness alone, whose form is supreme bliss.
To you who delight in the Self, who are peaceful, and whose vision of duality has ceased—to you, who are all forms, salutations again and again.
Salutations to you, the great Hṛṣīkeśa, whose form is infinite; in whom this universe exists, from whom it arises, and before whom it is born.
Salutations to You, that Brahman, who bears the earth made of clay; whom the mind, intellect, senses, and vital breaths neither touch nor know; who moves within and without like the sky—I bow to You.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Great Puruṣa, the Lord of the Great Elements, whose pair of lotus-feet are like the pollen of the lotuses that are the clusters of the modesty of all sentient beings, and who are the Supreme Lord through the lore known as Dharma; homage to you! And by means of this lore, Citraketu attained the state of a Vidyādhara.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-fifth chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—196.
Hari said: "Having recited the Vidyā known as Viṣṇudharma, he attained the status of Indra after completely conquering all his enemies; O Maheśvara, I shall describe that [Vidyā] to you."
One should place the syllables beginning with Oṃ in sequence upon the feet, knees, thighs, abdomen, heart, chest, mouth, and head.
Having recited "Namo Nārāyaṇāya" and likewise performed the reversal [of the syllables], one should then perform the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa) by means of the twelve-syllable vidyā.

One should assign the letters beginning with *praṇava* (oṃ) and ending with *ya* to the joints of the fingers and thumbs; one should place the *oṃkāra* at the heart and the entire mantra upon the head.
One should utter this mantra-assignment (mantranyāsa): "Oṃ, to Viṣṇu," placing Oṃ between the eyebrows, Śi at the eyes and so forth, up to the head.
One should meditate upon the supreme Self, which is endowed with the remaining powers; may Hari protect me, and in the form of the Fish, may he protect me in the water.
May Trivikrama protect me in the sky, may Vāmana protect me on land, may Narasiṃha protect me in the forest, and may Rāma protect me on the mountain.
May Varāha protect [me] on earth; may Nārāyaṇa protect [me] in the sky; may Kapila protect [me] from the bondage of karma; and may Datta protect [me] from disease.

Hayagrīva [attains his state] from the deities; Kumāra from the god who has the sea-monster as his banner (Kāmadeva); the god Nārada from the worship of others; and Kūrma always [arises] from the southwest (Nairṛta).
May Dhanvantari protect [me] from unwholesome food, Nāga from the power of anger, Yajña from all diseases, and Vyāsa from ignorance.
May the Buddha protect me from the assembly of heretics; may Kalki protect me from sin. May Viṣṇu protect me at midday; may Nārāyaṇa protect me in the morning.
May Madhuha protect me in the afternoon, and Mādhava in the evening; may Hṛṣīkeśa protect me at nightfall, and Janārdana at dawn.
May Śrīdhara protect [us] at midnight, and Padmanābha at the dead of night; may they, bearing the discus, the mace Kaumodakī, and arrows, slay our enemies and the Rākṣasas.
May the conch, the lotus, the Śārṅga bow, and likewise Garuḍa—who adorns His sides—protect my faculties of cognition, the mind, and the vital breaths from all enemies.
May Śeṣa, in his form as a serpent, protect me always and everywhere; and may Nārasiṃha always protect me in the intermediate directions and the cardinal points.
And whoever, maintaining this [mantra], beholds anyone with his eye, that person shall become submissive; moreover, being free from sin and released from disease, he shall go to heaven.

Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-sixth chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa. Dhanvantari said: I shall fully proclaim the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa], which was indeed uttered by Garuḍa for Kaśyapa; it is the Gāruḍa [treatise] by Sumitra, which destroys poison.
Earth, water, fire, air, and space—these classes within earth and the other elements are indeed the lords of the mandalas.
The deities residing within the five principles (pañcatattva) are attained by the servants of Viṣṇu; they are distinguished by long vowels and are devoid of neuter forms.

Śiva is said to possess six limbs: the heart, the head, and the crest-lock in sequence; then the armor, the eye, and the weapon. This is the ritual placement (nyāsa), which consists of their establishment in their respective locations.

At the end of the bestower of all accomplishments (sarvasiddhiprada), there is the fire of time (kālavahni) below the wind; it is conjoined with the sixth vowel and further endowed with the half-moon (ardhendu).
The divisions of the higher and lower are said to be above and below Śiva; one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon all the limbs with the letter *ra*, according to the prescribed rule.
By reciting [this mantra] in the heart, on the palm of the hand, upon the body, in the ear, or in the eye, one shall attain all perfections (siddhis) equal to those of the Four-faced One.
One should visualize the earth as square, very extensive, and yellow in color, presided over by the deity Indra; in its center is the mandala of Varuṇa.
In the center is a lotus likewise arranged, with a cool half-moon; it is gentle, with the luster of sapphire, or else it is a fiery mandala.
One should meditate upon a triangle joined with svastikas, blazing with garlands of flames, having a form like crushed collyrium, circular, and adorned with a bindu.
One should meditate upon the nectar of space, which has the appearance of waves of milk, possesses the luster of pure crystal, and is flooding the entire world.
Vāsuki and Śaṅkhapāla are stationed in the circle of the earth; Karkoṭaka and Padmanābha are established in the western quarter.
In the southeast, one should also place Kulika and Takṣaka, as well as Mahābja and Kauravya; these five beings, situated within the wind-maṇḍala, should be installed.
One should place Jayā and likewise Vijayā upon the joints of the fingers, starting from the thumb to the little finger, in both direct and reverse order.

Having assigned the six limbs of Śiva to the locations of one's own mouth and so forth, one should assign them to the little finger and the rest, to the heart and the rest, to the crest-lock, and to the two hands.

One should first perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-nyāsa) in sequence upon the joints of the fingers; then follows the placement of the elements (bhūta-nyāsa), and likewise the placement of the limbs of Śiva (śivāṅga-nyāsa).
The procedure for the installation and worship of all mantras is said to consist of the *praṇava* at the beginning, the name itself at the end, and being accompanied by that very name.
The first syllable of their names is proclaimed to be this mantra; it is the mantra that brings about the presence of the eight classes of nāgas.
Oṃ svāhā, preceded by the five elements in their proper order—this is Tārkṣya himself, the accomplisher of all rites.

Having performed the ritual placement (*karanyāsa*) upon the body with the vowels, one should again perform the placement [of the consonants]; one should contemplate the vital breath (*prāṇa*) as blazing, which effects the purification of the self.

Afterwards, one should contemplate the seed-syllable, which is of the nature of nectar until the end of the year; having thus performed the nourishment, one should contemplate it upon the crown of one's own head.
One should offer the earth, shining with the luster of molten gold, filled with all the worlds and accompanied by the guardians of the quarters, at one’s feet.
The wise practitioner should place this blessed Earth within his own body; he should meditate upon it as being dark-colored, and it becomes twice the size of the physical earth.
Having placed within the space between the navel and the neck the triangular mandala of the Sun, blazing and filled with garlands of flames reaching as far as the world of Brahmā;
One should meditate upon the sharp mandala of Vāyu, which resembles the appearance of crushed collyrium, pervading and abiding within the entire body, situated in the form of one's own self.
Situated above the topknot, it is divine, possessing the luster of pure crystal, pervading the immeasurable great void, and like nectar.

Having first performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the elements and the serpents in their proper order, one should apply the mantras ending in the letter *la* and joined with the nasal bindu according to the sequence of the elements.

Then one should offer the seed-syllable of Śiva, and thereafter meditate upon the maṇḍala. The wise practitioner who knows the sequence prescribed for whichever maṇḍala—that knower of the ritual rules should contemplate its specific color at the time of performing the rite.
Then, one should constantly meditate upon Tārkṣya, adorned with fluttering black serpents as his wings, for the sake of neutralizing both stationary and mobile poisons.
Having surrounded [the practitioner] with planets, spirits, piśācas, ḍākinīs, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and nāgas, one should place Śiva within one's own body.

The placement [of mantras] for the nāgas and the two classes of beings is declared to be twofold; having meditated thus, one should perform the ritual actions in sequence, beginning with the principle of the self (ātmatattva).
Having first offered the three principles (tritattva), and thereafter the principle of Śiva (sivatattva), just as [they are] in the body, so too in the deity, upon the joints of the fingers.

Having first performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon the body in both direct and reverse order—namely the bulb (kanda), the stalk (nāla), the lotus (padma), as well as virtue (dharma), knowledge (jñāna), and so forth.
One should worship with the letter at the end of the class conjoined with the second vowel; "śauṃ" is in the center of the pericarp, and on the head [of the deity] it is joined with the letter *ra*.

One should place the groups beginning with *a*, *ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *ta*, *pa*, *ya*, and *śa* starting from the east; likewise, two by two, ending at the petals and the filaments, starting from the east.

One should place the vowels upon the filaments and worship the sixteen [deities] ending with Īśāna; the powers (śaktis) beginning with Vāmā have been declared, and thereafter one should place the three principles (tattvas).
Then, one should invoke Śiva at the crown of the head; thereafter, one should place the Lord together with his limbs (the *aṅgas*) upon the pericarp (*karṇikā*), preceded by the preliminary rites.
One should worship Earth on the western petal, Water situated on the northern petal, Fire on the southern petal, and Vāyu on the eastern petal.
One should first visualize one's own seed-syllable in the form of the deity as previously described; *yaṃ* is the root of the wind in the southwest, while the syllable *ra* resides in the fire.
And one should always worship Vaṃ as the Lord; one should worship Oṃ situated in the heart, and one should worship those subtle elements (tanmātras) and gross elements (bhūtamātras) only outside.
Thereafter, having meditated upon the limbs of Śiva, one should then worship them: having worshipped the heart in the southeast, the head in the region of the northeast;
One should place the *śikhā* in the southwest (*nairṛtya*), assign the *kavaca* in the northwest (*vāyavya*), place the *astra* on the exterior, and position the *netra* in the north (*uttara*).
One should worship the seed-syllables at the tips of the petals and at the center of the pericarp; the eight nāgas, beginning with Ananta and ending with Kulīra, are situated there in sequence.
The mantra-practitioner should always worship, according to the ritual procedure, each one individually in order starting from the east and ending with Īśa.
This rite is prescribed for the heart-lotus according to the ritual rules, as well as upon a stone or a consecrated mandala; it is to be performed both daily and on occasional occasions.
One should constantly contemplate the Self, which can assume any form at will and is captivating, flooding the entire universe and being the agent of both creation and dissolution.
Blazing with garlands of flames reaching to the end of the world of Brahmā, he has ten arms, four faces, tawny eyes, and holds a trident in his hand.

For the sake of attaining siddhi in all rites, one should meditate upon Bhairava, who has terrifying fangs, is exceedingly fierce, possesses three eyes, and bears the moon upon his crest; and likewise, one should meditate upon Garuḍa.
For the purpose of destroying the nāgas, he manifested the terrifying and formidable Garuḍa; his two feet were established in the netherworld (pātāla), and the directions were supported by his wings.
One should contemplate the seven heavens upon his chest, the cosmic egg resting upon his throat, and his head extending from the east to the northeast.
He who dwells within the crest of Sadāśiva, who is indeed the triad of powers, the Śiva higher than the highest, Tārkṣya himself, the manifest leader of the worlds.
Three-eyed and of fierce form, the destroyer of poisonous serpents, the devourer with a terrifying mouth—Garuḍa, whose very body is the mantra.

In all ritual actions, one should contemplate [the deity] as blazing like the fire of time (kālāgni). Having thus performed the rite of placement (nyāsa), whatever one contemplates in the mind, that shall come to pass.

Whatever may be the goal to be accomplished, a man indeed becomes like Garuḍa; by his mere sight, pretas, bhūtas, yakṣas, nāgas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas, as well as quartan fevers and other ailments, are destroyed.
Dhanvantari said: Thus he spoke to Garuḍa, and Garuḍa spoke it to Kaśyapa; hear now that knowledge just as Maheśvara spoke it to Gaurī.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-seventh chapter in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the first part of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa— [Chapter 198].

Bhairava said: Now I shall declare the *Nityaklinnā*, the *Tripurā* who bestows both worldly enjoyment (*bhukti*) and liberation (*mukti*).
