Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: She who was the daughter of Soma in a previous creation, though remaining in her father’s house, that virtuous woman indeed made her own birth meaningful by serving Viṣṇu together with her father.
She constantly listened to the true Purāṇas and always performed prostrations at the feet of Viṣṇu; performing the remembrance of Viṣṇu, the Deliverer, she always circumambulated him.

But that maiden, filled with world-weariness from hearing [the teachings], became detached along with her father; she renounced her hair, her friend, the elephant and other [possessions], priceless jewels, her home, and everything else.

He indeed considered all this to be perishable, dependent upon himself, and fashioned by Hari; and since sons, friends, and the like were given by Him alone, they were likewise taken away by Him, yet he felt no pain.

This very day, Viṣṇu, the supreme compassionate one, has shown mercy toward me, though you did not do so well; for that maiden, along with her father, O Lord of Sages, has indeed entered the eternally pure Vāsudeva.

O Lord of the Twice-born, because that goddess had approached with perfect devotion and spontaneity, she did not conceive of any means of subsistence for herself; rather, she acted as if she were already established in her goal from the very beginning.

She indeed made her wealth consist solely in the lotus-feet of Viṣṇu, which carry one across the ocean of suffering; and she properly employed her faculty of speech, O bird, always in the description of the qualities of Hari.

The Goddess performed the cleansing of Viṣṇu’s body with her hands during the sweeping of his dwelling; and she applied her ears to the arising of Hari’s sacred stories, which are like nectar and lead to the path of liberation and other goals.

The eye is for beholding images and the like, removing the impurities accumulated since beginningless time; the skin is for touching true Vaiṣṇavas, as well as for contact with the remains of offerings (nirmālya), fragrances, and unguents.

She directed her sense of smell toward the essence of Hari’s feet, which grants liberation from saṃsāra; and her sense of taste toward the remnants of Hari’s food offerings, mixed with the auspicious *tulasī* and other ingredients.

Their feet move along the paths to the sacred fields of Hari; their heads bow in worship at the feet of Hṛṣīkeśa; and with hearts and mouths full of the desire for service to Hari, such people devoted to Him of Excellent Renown conduct themselves.
He fixed his mind upon Nishkamarupa, and the organ of speech undertook the act of praise; thus, he constantly offered the entire collection of his activities at the feet of the Supreme Lord.

He went with his father for the purpose of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites (tīrthas) specifically to please Lord Hari; first, having honored the brahmins who were devotees of Viṣṇu at home with garments, ornaments, and other gifts.
Afterwards, the Goddess made a vow before Viṣṇu for the sake of a pilgrimage: "O Mukunda, for as long as the pilgrimage lasts, I shall remain a perpetual celibate."

For as long as I shall perform this pilgrimage, may there be association with Vaiṣṇavas and the hearing of the stories of Hari; and may there be no physical contact with those who are not Vaiṣṇavas, nor even the company of those who are not followers of Mukunda.
O Mukunda, I shall never undertake long journeys with my friends, sons, or other loved ones; O Mukunda, keep far away from the company of those who perform pilgrimages out of worldly desire.

What do the noble ones say is the fruit for those who undertake a pilgrimage while completely disregarding the Śālagrāma? Whenever there is the sight of sacred fords (tīrthas), one should at that very time place the Śālagrāma before oneself.

O Lord of Birds, the noble ones say that if one performs a pilgrimage to sacred sites on foot, the full fruit is obtained; however, if one undertakes a pilgrimage to sacred sites while wearing footwear or using protective sandals for the feet, they say that pilgrimage is deficient by half.

If one performs a pilgrimage while seated upon a vehicle or a horse, the merit is said to be reduced by half; if on a vehicle such as a bull, it is said to be reduced to a quarter; and if eating the food of others, they say it is rendered useless.

There is no fault whatsoever in eating the food of others for great-souled ascetics who know the Vedas; having resolved this with the utmost reverence, she departed for the purpose of a pilgrimage to sacred sites.

Having first bathed and discarded the fragrance of Hari’s remains, he indeed performed the ritual hearing [of the scriptures]; and having also taken his meal together with his father, he traveled one krośa on the following day.

There, having honored the twice-born with food and drink, the Goddess caused them to hear the truth during the night. The noble ones declare that the pilgrimage of those who thus perform the journey constantly shall be fruitful.

"O Lord of Birds, the great ones have said that a pilgrimage to sacred sites is useless without compassion; O Lord of Birds, those who do not listen to the divine stories of Hari by day or by night while on the path to a sacred site [attain nothing]."

Know that the journey of his horses and other mounts was indeed rendered utterly futile; declare the fault of the horses and so forth, for the destruction of sin occurs through the sight of the Gaṅgā and other sacred sites.

The destruction of sin occurs from the sight of Viṣṇu residing in a sacred field; speak of the offense even of a cat [in this regard]. The destruction of sin occurs from the worship of Viṣṇu residing in a sacred field; speak of the offense of those who perform such worship.

For those performing recitations and other rites, the destruction of sin occurs, and from the meditation on Viṣṇu, the destruction of poverty happens instantly; however, they say that everything performed without focused contemplation (anusandhāna) is indeed entirely useless.

Therefore, O lord of birds, having heard this story of Hari which destroys all sins, one shall become a devotee of Viṣṇu; and having seen, again and again, that which is marked with the footprints of Hari, and having remembered it, again and again, one shall become a devotee, O lord of birds.
O lord of sages, that maiden also went with her father to behold Śrīnivāsa residing on Śeṣācala; and along the way, she meditated upon Hari, the Lord of Ramā.
When shall I behold the broad chest of Śrīnivāsa, adorned with the jewel Śrīvatsa? When shall I behold the beautiful belly of Śrīnivāsa, marked by the three folds of skin?

When shall I behold the neck of Śrīnivāsa, which resembles a conch shell and is the refuge of Maharloka? When shall I behold the navel of Śrīnivāsa, which is ever the refuge of the intermediate space (Antarikṣa) and is perfectly full?
When indeed shall I behold the face of Murāri, which is the eternal refuge of Janaloka?
When shall I behold the head of Śrīnivāsa, the eternal refuge of the world of truth? When shall I behold the waist of Śrīnivāsa, the eternal refuge of the earthly realm?
When shall I behold the broad palm of Śrīnivāsa, which is the eternal refuge of Sutala? And when shall I behold the very tender knee of Śrīnivāsa, which is the refuge of Talātala?

When shall I behold the shanks of Śrīnivāsa, which have always been the refuge of the netherworld? When shall I behold the soles of Hari’s feet, which have always been the refuge of the realm of Pātāla?
While reflecting thus on the path, the queen beheld Lord Śeṣa upon Śeṣācala, resplendent with his thousand hoods, amidst various trees, monkeys, and female monkeys.

"By the accumulation of merit acquired over infinite births, this supreme mountain has indeed been seen by me today; at the sight of it, her eyes clouded with tears, she immediately rose and bowed her head."

Having looked at his face, she should perform a bow; she should not perform a bow by turning her back toward him or other parts of the body. She too performed a bow twelve times, having placed the Śālagrāma before him.

Thus, the Vaiṣṇavas must perform the rites for Parvata, while you, indeed, must perform them in the opposite manner. Śrīnivāsa, who dwells within honey, resides eternally on the mountain and is worshipped by Ramā, Brahmā, and the other gods.

"I shall see the most excellent, supreme abode of Śrī, and then I shall indeed ascend the mountain. Having spoken thus, she established her residence at the holy ford named Kapila together with her father.

Right here dwells Śrīnivāsa, Hari himself, neither by means of material substance nor in any other form. Having first bathed there and performed the tonsure, one should cause the *tīrtha-śrāddha* to be performed at that excellent sacred site (*sutīrtha*).

Having given away all her possessions, such as cows, land, and gold, the virtuous woman then ascended the mountain; having installed a Śālagrāma stone at the front, she too prostrated once more with great devotion.
Having thus ascended as far as the hundredth step, she sat down there; she listened to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa and heard the praises of Veṅkaṭādri.
From his preceptor Jaigīṣavya, he heard with great devotion the entire truth concerning the mountain Veṅkaṭādri.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "Description of the Procedure for the Pilgrimage to Veṅkaṭeśagiri," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
The glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Chapter 24.

Jaigīṣavya said: O maiden of smiling countenance, listen to you regarding the merit of ascending this mountain named Veṅkaṭa; indeed, all people who perform the ascent while reciting the Śrī Gītā attain [great merit].

At every step, the Lord Śrīnivāsa is indeed fully, fully pleased with the host of his devotees; by pleasing him, they all attain liberation. When Hari is satisfied, O maiden, what is there that cannot be obtained?

When one hears the Purāṇa in the vicinity of a staircase, then a pilgrimage to all sacred fords and other holy sites has been accomplished; then, during the day, they always extol Hari, Śrīnivāsa, and the Guru here on the path.
Having heard of the greatness of the steps and having established the Śālagrāma there, that virtuous woman bowed down once more and then ascended the steps.

O Lord of Birds, by ascending the steps of those who are not Vaiṣṇavas, there is no pleasing of Hari; rather, O Lord of Birds, that very act serves only to cast them further into the blinding darkness.
In various places, the Goddess spoke thus once more regarding Jaigīṣavya; the maiden said: "Jaigīṣavya is Śrīnivāsa, for Hari, as Śrīnivāsa, is seen by Brahmā and the other gods."
"O Jaigīṣavya, out of compassion, please speak. Thus addressed, Jaigīṣavya spoke to Hari, the daughter of Soma, the virtuous Satī, and said: "Śrīnivāsa is seen by Brahmā and the other gods."

Venkatesha is seen by Rudra and the other gods as possessing a splendor exceeding that of a hundred thousand suns; Shrinivasa is seen by Rudra and the others with a brilliance surpassing the combined luster of a million suns.
The Lord of Ramā, whose splendor surpasses a thousand suns, appears like the moon to sages and others; yet to virtuous men, Hari is directly perceived.

Lord Śrīnivāsa is always seen like a star, for Hari is directly perceived by the sages; yet that Lord of Veṅkaṭa, Śrīnivāsa, is seen like the sun by those in the cycle of worldly existence, O King of Birds.

Indeed, the light [of the deity] appears as if it were a collection of essences; to those who follow false paths, Śrīnivāsa appears like a stone, manifesting a dark-blue form that is seen merely as a rock in the Kali age.

In the Kali age, Hari is indeed Śrīnivāsa for all men, and the Goddess is the very form of Śrīnivāsa; yet no humans recognize this, because in the Kali age they are all characterized by tamas and rajas.

Indeed, only a few who associate with them are truly sattvic; thus, devotees are indeed rare in the Kali age. Those who appear to be devotees are not actually devotees, for they are merely intent on filling their bellies and supporting their wives and children.

They undertake pilgrimages for that very purpose; indeed, devotion and knowledge are difficult to attain in the Kali age. For those devotees who are never dispassionate, the vision of Hari is likewise difficult to obtain.

O King of Birds, I shall describe the true nature of your devotee: one who is full of knowledge and exceedingly affectionate toward you, yet not bound by hatred; such a person is endowed with devotion. Now listen as I correctly explain your various forms of hatred.

The notion that the soul, which is eternally dependent, is distinct from Hari—who is independent, non-material, and fully replete with knowledge and bliss—and the thought that Hari is incomplete in his qualities, constitute [the two forms of ignorance].

The constant concern for the honor of the gods, such as Brahmā and Rudra, as well as that of the twice-born, and the perpetual contemplation of the superiority of Brahmā, Rudra, and others over Viṣṇu, is indeed hatred.

O Bhadrā, the great ones say that perceiving a distinction between the hands, feet, and other limbs of Viṣṇu is hatred; likewise, thinking of the cutting or piercing of his incarnations is considered even a thought of death.

The noble ones say that hating those who are devoted to Him and criticizing His words is indeed hatred itself; moreover, those seen in the world who are possessed by hatred are never found to be His devotees.

The maiden said: "O Jaigīṣavya, tell me who these devotees are and how they manifested their devotion; for Hari, the abode of Śrī, the Great-Souled One, is always compassionate toward the assembly of his devotees and their protector."

Thus addressed, the high-souled Jaigīṣavya, the best among devotees, spoke while remembering the maiden. Jaigīṣavya said: "Prahlāda and others were devotees of Śrīnivāsa, having indeed cultivated supreme devotion toward Nṛsiṃha."
Parāśara, a devotee of the Abode of Śrī, having offered his devotion to Hari in the form of Vyāsa, subsequently attained unsurpassed sovereignty and obtained knowledge from Nṛsiṃha.

Having praised the reality of knowledge through that [practice] and having attained it, Nārada—whose soul was nourished by devotion and who was a devotee of Śrīnivāsa—went to liberation after having practiced devotion toward Hari even while in the womb.

Through that devotion he attained the status of being a son of Brahmā, and through the acquisition of knowledge, he went to liberation—he who was indeed Ambarīṣa, a devotee of Śrīnivāsa, having practiced devotion toward Hari, the supreme deity.

Having chanted and attained wisdom, Durvāsas also attained liberation, his soul nourished by that; and Mucukunda, a devotee of Śrīnivāsa, having cultivated firm devotion through detachment, likewise reached it.

Having attained knowledge of the reality of Viṣṇu, that high-souled Puṇḍarīka, whose self was nourished by that [knowledge], obtained liberation; for he was a devotee of Śrīnivāsa who, being commanded by his father, practiced devotion to Viṣṇu.

Through the grace of Hari, he whose soul was nourished by devotion attained unsurpassed knowledge and liberation; and Brahmā, Vāyu, Sarasvatī, and all those of upright yoga should be known [to have likewise attained these].

They are indeed those whose devotion to Murāri is ever unbroken, who are not attached to desire, and who possess pure forms; they are the deities known as Girīśa, Nāgeśa, and Khageśa, as well as Śukra, Ārka, Guru, Candra, and Indusūrya.
Varuṇa, Agni, Manu, Dharma, Kubera, Vighneśa, the Nāsatyas, and the hosts of Maruts, as well as Parjanya, Mitra, and all others—these are indeed always the devotees of Śrīnivāsa.
Viśvāmitra, Bhṛgu, Aurva, Kutsa, Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Kratu, Śakti, Vasiṣṭha, Sautamīya, Pulastya, and Bhāradvāja are the devotees of Śrīnivāsa.

Māndhātṛ, Nahuṣa, Ambarīṣa, Sagara, King Pṛthu, Haihaya, Ikṣvāku, Bharata, the two sons of Yayāti, Dharma, Vikukṣi, Uttāna, Bibhīṣaṇa, and Daśaratha—these great men of supreme knowledge are always remembered as devotees of the illustrious Lord of Veṅkaṭa and their Guru.
The Bhāgīrathī, the ocean, the Yamunā, and the Sarasvatī; the Godāvarī, the Narmadā, the Kṛṣṇā, and likewise the Bhīmarathī.
The Sarayū, Phalgu, Kāverī, Gaṇḍakī, and Kapilā—these, O beautiful lady, are also devotees of Hari who reside right here.
O maiden, listen as I explain the intention behind this, while I am present: wherever the discourse concerning the Great-Souled Viṣṇu proceeds upon the path.
Wherever Vaiṣṇavas who awaken one to the true meaning of the reality of Hari reside, there all devotees likewise abide in Viṣṇu.

Those who perform the divine procession with contemplation of the Supreme Self are the devotees of Hari, and none other; for, O Lord of Birds, every duty of the Vaiṣṇavas finds its ultimate fulfillment in Hari alone.
Having reached Śeṣācala, he who, being devoid of devotion, does not offer food, clothing, ornaments, and the like—who indeed is a more base beast than he?

O Goddess, the devotees of Hari reside on the Śrīnivāsa mountain and in various other places in the form of the Gaṅgā and so forth, for the sake of serving the Lord of Wide Strides; therefore, no worship should ever be performed for them.

I shall state the intended meaning there; listen to it in that context. Even those [deities] mentioned in the Purāṇas should be worshipped individually with garments, perfumes, incense, and so forth; and having seen them, the wise man indeed should pay homage.

O Goddess, one should salute the feet of virtuous Brahmins with both hands joined in the *añjali* gesture; likewise, one should perform an eight-limbed prostration (*aṣṭāṅga-vandana*) to Viṣṇu and to the Guru, regarding them with the same consciousness as Viṣṇu.

One must indeed perform prostration with the eight limbs (aṣṭāṅga-vandana) to the Gaṅgā and other such rivers, as well as to tulasī plants; one must likewise bow to aśvattha trees, and pay homage to cows and other such beings mentally.

The worship of Viṣṇu, the God of gods, must always be performed with devotion by Vaiṣṇavas alone and not by others; O maiden, those who possess the Name, who are wise, and who are truly devoted, must always perform the worship of Viṣṇu.

O maiden, those who are named thus and possess knowledge and great devotion must always perform the worship of Viṣṇu; but those who are named thus and are devotees of Viṣṇu, O Goddess, must never perform the worship of Viṣṇu here.

Indeed, he who worships the God of gods out of delusion and the like goes to the blinding darkness of great unrighteousness; for it was Hari who gave the names of Brahmā and others to the goddess, while Viṣṇu gave his own names to the inhabitants of heaven.
"O maiden, the wise king did not take Keśava and the others with him, but abandoned his own city and departed; thus I have told you all this, O maiden—this supreme truth must be properly upheld."
"O Govinda, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava! You all must worship me in every way. Then, O Lord of Birds, they all gathered together once more and, chanting these names, ascended Mount Vaikuṇṭha.
Previously chanting the names of Hari there and savoring the name of Śrīnivāsa, they all likewise acted to behold Śrīnivāsa, making a sound like the clapping of palms as they cried out.

Having heard these words of Kṛṣṇa, Tārkṣya said to Kṛṣṇa: "How did they taste [it]? Please explain this in detail. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "O Śrīnivāsa, Your very name is this name; indeed, the Lord is the name itself. Because Brahmā and the others take refuge in Her, She obtained the names 'Ramā' and 'Śrī'."
Because he is the eternal and absolute refuge of Ramā, Hari is known by the name Śrīnivāsa. O Śrīnivāsa! Thus they cry out, their hair standing on end and clapping their hands in joy.
Today itself let us behold the face of this Hari; when shall we have fulfilled our purpose? O Keśava, having shown us Your lotus feet even today, please show us great compassion!

They call him Brahmā, they call him the Ancient One; they call him the one denoted by the syllable *ka*, the Lord of all worlds; and they call him Īśa, Arha, and Rudra—the impeller in the acts of creation and dissolution.
Therefore, calling out "O Keśava! and making Hari, whose name is Keśava, dance, they went toward the pool of bliss, flowing with joy; indeed, they went while crying out, "Nārāyaṇa!"

Therefore, because He is the locus of those defects, their opposites—the qualities—and the *nārās*, He is Murāri; O Lord of Birds, they call Him Nārāyaṇa here in this world because of His connection with the *nārās*, for all are liberated through Him.

O Lord of Sages, because they are the refuge, they are called *nāra*; therefore, even more so than them, he alone is Nārāyaṇa. And those who are liberated have entered his footstep, which is the water of the cosmic egg, by the mere glance of his eye.

O Lord of Birds, because that which was born is *nārāḥ* (the waters), and because you are their eternal refuge, O Lord of Beings, people here in the world call you *Nārāyaṇa*, for you are the creator of infinite cosmic eggs (*brahmāṇḍa*).

Thus they danced, praising Govinda, for there is indeed nothing else nor even a vision [of Him]; since all speech is denoted by the word "go" (cow), and He is established by all those "gobhiḥ" (rays/words).
Therefore, O Bhīma, they always remember you as Govinda and likewise as Vedavedya; for, filled with tears of joy, they did not dance before Hari, the slayer of Mura, at the mere sight of you.
"O Lord, grant that your servants and maidservants may always reside in the fourteenth world; for you yourself dwell thus, and as Vāsudeva, you sport here eternally at all times."
Because the great ones have thus called him "O God," they likewise call Hari "Vāsudeva. "O Vāsudeva! they all danced at all times, and "O Mādhava! they all indeed danced.
Everyone says, "O Lord of Lakṣmī," because the word "Dhanin" (the wealthy one) refers to oneself; for this reason, the noble ones call you "Mādhava. O Lord of Lakṣmī, likewise protect your devotees!

Speaking thus, they danced and moved along, chanting such names as "O Viṣṇu, protect us always and eternally; because you are spread everywhere," and so forth. Endowed with devotion and remembering Śrīnivāsa, they all proceeded and beheld the sacred ford (tīrtha).

The maiden said: "O Lord of Sages, what is the name of this sacred ford? O Master of the Accomplished, tell us what purpose is served here. For whom is the Blessed Śrīnivāsa pleased at this excellent holy site? Speak of it in detail."

Jaigīṣavya said: O maiden, listen; there was once a man of great intelligence named Prahlāda, the foremost among the devotees of Hari. With a mind free from desire, he went to behold Śrīnivāsa, who resides on the Śeṣa mountain.
In this place, the Lord questioned the sons of the Daityas regarding the true nature of Hari: "O maiden, worship Śrīnivāsa in the form of Nṛsiṃha; human birth is extremely difficult to attain."

Even there, O best of Daityas, the true reality of Viṣṇu Nṛhari is very difficult to attain, and likewise is a proper pilgrimage. In whatever place, during whatever pilgrimage, the story of Hari is told—[that is where the goal lies].
"In that place Hari always resides, for Nṛsiṃha is indeed pervading everywhere. Having heard this, those sons of the Daityas spoke to Prahlāda, the foremost of devotees of Hari.
"O friend, if Hari pervades all, why indeed is Nṛsiṃha not seen here in the form of water? Being thus addressed by the sons of the Dānavas, he praised Viṣṇu with the utmost reverence.
"Reveal your true form to me, in a form suitable for the sons of the Dānavas. Thus praised, Hari, the Abode of Śrī, assumed an underwater form within that [water].

Those who perform their ablutions in this sacred ford shall possess supreme and firm knowledge; yet, O dear one, in this regard, human beings will certainly lack the understanding, especially in the Kali age.

Having granted the boon to the best of the Daityas, Viṣṇu vanished into the excellent basin filled with water; even today Nṛsiṃha remains within that water, as does Prahlāda along with the sons of the Daityas.

At that excellent bathing place, in every direction and at various spots, the cry of "Victory! is heard throughout the afternoon. This sacred ford is named Nārasiṃha; indeed, men should perform their ablutions here during the maiden period of the moon.
Having bathed at that sacred ford and having properly offered an excellent lamp to a preeminent brahmin, they proceeded toward Śrīnivāsa once more to behold him, crying out, "Govinda, Govinda!"
Having reached the place presided over by the chief vital breath (mukhyaprāṇa), the Goddess entered there and said: "Tell me how Jaigīṣavya may behold Viṣṇu, the abode of Śrī; explain that to me."

Jaigīṣavya, with a joyful heart, said: "O maiden, listen as I speak this tantra; having heard it from me, perform everything I have instructed, after first beholding the primordial gateway of Śrīnivāsa."
Thousands of offenses are committed by me day and night; O God, Supreme Person, forgive them all for me.
O Mādhava, reduce to ashes all my mental, verbal, and physical faults in every respect—those which cause hatred toward the Vaiṣṇavas.

O Goddess, one should properly remember the first gate of Śrīnivāsa as indeed victory and triumph; O Goddess, at the sacrifice of Dakṣa, one should likewise properly remember Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa of Śrīnivāsa.
O Goddess, one should devoutly remember Nanda and Sunanda at the western side of Śrīnivāsa; and at the left door of Śrīnivāsa, O daughter, one should remember Kumudākṣa and Kumudanta.
And when shall I, O Goddess, behold with devotion and great reverence one who enters the temple with devotion, performs twelve circumambulations, and at every step remembers the Abode of Śrī?
O Goddess, having properly sipped water for purification at Śrīsvāmitīrtha, and having bathed and bowed to Bhūvarāha, one should enter the gateway with devotion while uttering, "Govinda, Govinda."

Afterwards, one should perform prostration to Hari in the form of the eight-limbed salutation (aṣṭāṅga-namaskāra) and enter the temple of the deity. Standing again at the entrance, one should meditate mentally upon the deities seated upon their pedestals.

In the center, one should fully prostrate to the Śrīnivāsa-pīṭha and the goddess Nārāyaṇī. To the left of the deity, outside the area of the pīṭha, one should likewise offer salutations to the Guru-deva.

O Lord of Birds, one should indeed prostrate in the south-eastern corner at the front and lower part of the pedestal; O Goddess, in the south-western quarter, the Vaiṣṇava Vyāsadeva is always to be saluted.

With a soul nourished by devotion, one should first pay homage to Sudurgā in the northwest corner; then, above the pedestal in the southeast corner, [one should offer] "Salutation to Yama, the presiding deity of Dharma."

Above the pedestal, in the upper corner of the southwest (Nairṛta), one should bow to Vāyu, the Lord of Knowledge; and above the pedestal, in the northwest (Vāyu) corner, to Subhrū and Rudra, the Lord of the passions of detachment (vairāgya).

O Goddess, one should bow to Indra, the lord of the sovereign powers, in the northeast corner above the pedestal; and O Goddess, one should bow to Aryaman, the lord of the Aryamans, here in the southeast of the pedestal.

To the south of the deity and the pedestal, one should bow to Durgā, who is known as Ugrarūpā; and to the west of the pedestal, one should indeed prostrate to Kāmadeva, the lord of those who possess health.

To the north of the deity’s seat, one should meditate upon Rudradeva as the lord of the [nine] powers; and in the center of the seat, O maiden, one should always bow down to Varāha, who is known as the Supreme Puruṣa.
Above that, one should always bow to Lakṣmī, who is known as Śakti and whose form is the support; above her, one should bow to Vāyu and Kūrma; and above them, one should bow to Śeṣa and Kūrma.

Above that, one with beautiful eyebrows should indeed bow to Bhūdevatā, the presiding deity of the earth; and above her, one should meditate upon the god Varuṇa, the sovereign lord of the Ocean of Milk.

Above that, one should indeed bow down and worship Lakṣmī and the two maidens known as Śvetadvīpa; above that, one should indeed bow down and worship the great divine Lakṣmī and the one named Maṇḍapa.

In the center of the pedestal, one should worship the one known as Yama and Lakṣmī; and in the middle of Yama, one should worship the Goddess. To the right of the god Yama, O auspicious lady, one should pay homage to Sūrya in the form of a lamp.
One should bow to the goddess Śrī in the form of a lamp on the left side of the god Yama, and one should also bow to the fire-god Agni in the form of a lamp at the front of the god Yama.

One should bow before the Lord to the goddess named Bhūmi, who presides over the principle of *tattva*, and constantly remember her; one should likewise bow to Durgā, who presides over *tamas*, in the form of the couch of Śrīnivāsa Viṣṇu.

O Goddess, one should bow to the single Self, which has the form of the steps of the pedestal extending toward the east and other directions; and O Daughter, one should likewise bow to that which consists of knowledge, having the form of the steps of the pedestal situated in the southern direction.

O Goddess, on the eastern petal of the lotus, one should pay homage to this one called Strīrūpā and the one called Vimalā; O Goddess, listen now as I describe the homage to Brahmā and the other deities on the petal situated in the southeast corner.

One should bow to the supreme goddess named Utkarṣaṇā, as well as to Indrāṇī, Brahmā, Vāyu, and Śeṣa; and on the eight petals of the lotus situated upon Dakṣa, one should worship those beginning with Nārāyaṇa, Ākāra, and Śeṣa.
O maiden, one must indeed perform prostration to those in female forms on the western petal; likewise to Gopāla, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Vāyu, the Brahmins and others, as well as Śeṣa, Rudra, and the rest.

One must indeed perform salutation to those in female forms on the petals located in the northeast corner; [this applies] to Īśāna, Nārāyaṇa, up to Viriñca, as well as Vāyu, Viyat, Śeṣa, the gods, and the rest.

One must likewise perform prostration to those in female forms and to the center of the lotus; there resides the goddess Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī, known as Anugrahā, who is the source of grace for Vāyu, Vyoman, Śeṣa, Rudra, and the others.

One must indeed perform obeisance to those in female form, for they constitute the very nature of the excellent seat of yoga (*suyogapīṭha*). One should always bow to the one known as Śrī Ananta, and likewise to the god who is the abode of Śrī.
A wise person should bow to Lakṣmī on the left side of Śrīnivāsa, and to auspicious Dharā on the right side of Śrīnivāsa.
Outside the seat, in the eastern part, one should bow to the auspicious Kṛpolka; likewise, one should bow to Maholka in the south and Vīrolka in the west.
And one should pay homage to the North, and to the great-souled Ulkā; the wise person should also bow to Sahasrolkā in all four corners.
One should pay homage to Vāsudeva in the east, to the god Saṃkarṣaṇa in the south, and to Pradyumna in the west.
In the north, one should tirelessly pay homage to Aniruddha; and in the southeast, O auspicious maiden, one should always pay homage to Māyā.
One should pay homage to Jayā in the southwest and also to Vāyu in the northwest; one should likewise pay homage to Kṛtyā in the northeast and to the one named Śānti in the southeast.
One should pay homage to Keśava in the east, and likewise to Nārāyaṇa; one should offer salutations to Mādhava in the southwest and also in the northwest.
In the southeast, one who is always pure and devoted should, with devotion, pay homage to the auspicious Kanyaka; likewise, one should bow to Govinda in the south and to Viṣṇu as well.
O girl, you should pay homage to Madhusūdana in the southwest (nairṛta), and likewise to Trivikrama and Vāmana in the west.
Then one should pay homage to Viṣṇu Śrīdhara with the syllable "Bhām"; and in the north, O Great Maiden, [one should say] "Salutation indeed to Hṛṣīkeśa."
Likewise, O beautiful lady, one should tirelessly pay homage to Padmanābha; and one should also pay homage to Dāmodara in the northeast.
In the fourth enclosure, one should offer salutation to Mahākūrma in the east; one should pay homage to Varāha in the auspicious southeast, O maiden.
In the south, one should offer salutations again and again to Nārasiṃha and Vāmana; in the southwest, one should pay homage to Bhārgava with a pure mind.
Then, one should likewise offer salutations to Mādhava and Kṛṣṇa in the west, and one should pay homage to Buddha in the auspicious northwest, O beautiful maiden.
In the north, one should pay homage with diligence to you who are infinite and have the form of a meteor; in the northeast, one should offer salutations to the one whose form is the universe.
One should bow to Vāruṇī in the southeast, Gāyatrī in the southwest, Bhāratī in the northwest, and Girijā in the northeast.
One should bow to Girijā on the left side, and likewise to Suparṇa; one should also pay homage to Indra in the east, together with his weapons.
"Salutations again and again to the attendant of Śrī Viṣṇu for the sake of acceptance; O Āgneya, salutations to you, Agni, together with your weapons," as before.
One should worship Yama in the south, Nirṛti in the southwest, Varuṇa in the west, and Vāyu with the salutation "Obeisance to Vāyu" in the northwest.
And in the north for Kubera, and in the northeast for Śiva; and between Īśāna and Śakra for Brahmā, together with his weapons.
And in the very center of Nirṛti, one should offer salutation again and again with "Obeisance, obeisance to Śeṣa. Having performed the salutation in this manner, one should prostrate repeatedly.
Thus has this entire system of philosophy been explained according to its rules; beyond this, however, O Lord of Ramā, you must proceed for the sake of further vision.

Having spoken thus, that goddess went joyfully with them, O bird. The procedure for the vision of Śrīnivāsa which was described must never be told to anyone, because it is to be kept secret at all times.

O Lord of Sages, the meeting with the virtuous who awaken one to the true nature of reality is indeed difficult to achieve; yet, through the accumulation of merit earned over many lifetimes, he attained union with his Guru.

Just as milk abandons its own transformation and the lotus sheds its remaining filth through contact with the one whose navel is a lotus, so too, through association with the virtuous, unstable dispositions shall cease and inauspicious things shall no longer exist.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Sequence for Ascending Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Hill and the Names of its Peaks and Devotees," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

At the gateway of Śrīnivāsa, that goddess, together with certain others, beheld the Svāmipuṣkariṇī. She meditated upon him—the savior of Brahmā and the other gods—exclaiming, "O Lord Hari! O Śrīnivāsa!"

For the sake of protection along with the gods, Viṣṇu is indeed eternally present in the waters of the Puṣkariṇī; therefore, they call it Svāmipuṣkariṇī, and there the maidens performed their ablutions.

O King of Birds, having become pure, the gods entered Śrīnivāsa’s abode with pure devotion to offer oblations; and the maidens, O King of Birds, performed everything exactly as instructed by their preceptor.
Then Hari revealed his own form, perfectly beautiful and complete, to her; that maiden beheld with devotion the form of Śrīnivāsa, which was enchanting to her mind.
Wearing a garment variegated with gold, he was putting on a tunic together with a turban.
The quarters of the sky were made fragrant by the scent of rut arising from the deer; he had eyes as broad as white lotuses, a neck like a conch shell, and mighty arms.
His body was adorned with a golden sacred thread; he resembled Kandarpa himself, possessing a beauty that deludes the world, with tender limbs that were utterly captivating.
And having seen him, the maiden rejoiced, her beautiful limbs bristling with thrill.

Her heart overflowing with the joy of seeing Him, her eyes brimming with tears of love and horripilation, the Goddess—her faults destroyed—danced before Viṣṇu with supreme devotion: "O Ānanda, protect me! O Mukunda, grant me happiness and protect me by bestowing liberation!"

Protect me always, O lotus-eyed one, with a gracious gaze moistened by the nectar of compassion! O Govinda, O Govinda, protect me, who am deeply afflicted, forever by granting the gift of knowledge and other virtues.

O Janārdana, having constantly avoided the most wicked attachments in the form of desire and the like, O Hari, O Hari, protect me always by subduing the powerful Daityas who take the form of obstacles.

O Rāmeśa, Lord of the four-faced one, Lord of the universe, protect me; O Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! O Rāmeśa, embodiment of the primal cause, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the hosts of Vṛndāraka gods, protect me!
Having thus bowed with supreme reverence, he praised Viṣṇu, the highest and most ancient; for O Lord, there are countless qualities in Viṣṇu that are never known even by Lakṣmī.

The qualities of Hari, which are of an exceedingly vast number, are indeed unknown to Lakṣmī even in the presence of those [gods]. Therefore, what power could there be for me in praising Hari? Nevertheless, I shall make an effort to praise You.

Through your grace, through the grace of Ramā, through the grace of Brahmā, through the grace of Bhāratīśa, and through the grace of Rudra, I shall offer this hymn of praise to you; nevertheless, O Viṣṇu, grant me peace.

If you are pleased with me, O Lord, grant me perpetual devotion at the soles of your feet; for by the sight of you, O God, my auspicious and inauspicious karma, as well as my constant misfortune, have been destroyed.

By your māyā, this world has been destroyed; intoxicated by pride, it has become deaf and blind. Indeed, through the power of your sovereignty, it has become mute toward those who are always humble, venerable, and elders.
Do not grant me unsurpassed sovereignty, which is contrary to the lotus of Your feet; O Lord, grant me instead the company of the virtuous who proclaim Your true nature.
O Vāsudeva, having burnt away my attachment to sons and other worldly things, grant me Your lotus feet; and having burnt away the anger directed toward true Vaiṣṇavas, grant me Your lotus feet.

Having burned away the greed for wealth and the like that is being committed, grant me [your grace] at the base of your lotus feet; and having burned away the delusion for sons and the like that is being committed, grant me [your grace] at the base of your lotus feet.

Having burnt away my learning, my son, my accumulated wealth, and my pride, grant me [Your] lotus feet at the base; having burnt away my envy along with the nature of the minds of true Vaiṣṇavas, protect me, O Lord of Veṅkaṭa!

And grant me a mantra, O you whose form is the primordial cause, by which there may be further union with you; I choose nothing other than union with your lotus feet—being gracious to me, grant that very thing to me.
Thus addressed, the gracious Lord Śrīnivāsa spoke, emitting nectar: "O maidens, recite right here this supreme mantra of most secret form with great reverence."

I shall speak the mantra with supreme reverence; listen today with devotion and supreme reverence! It consists of the final letter situated within [the gutturals], joined with the first [of the labials], likewise accompanied by the bindu, and conjoined with the first of the sparśas.

Joined with the letter *e*, ending in the first case (*prathamānta*), joined with a semi-vowel (*antastha*) in the third and fifth positions, conjoined with a sibilant (*ūṣman*), attached to the letter *ta*, joined with a vowel (*svara*) and a semi-vowel (*antastha*), and endowed with the syllable *oṃ* at both the beginning and the end.
"O maiden, by this mantra your desire shall indeed be fulfilled; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter. Having spoken thus, Śrīnivāsa Hari revealed his form in its entirety.
Having bowed to Śrīnivāsa, the goddess dwelt near Svāmisaras; on that day, she gratified all the brahmins and others with food possessing the six flavors.

In the evening, having seen Śrīnivāsa, the Goddess, with devotion, prostrated herself before him along with the manifestations of Śrīnivāsa in the form of his attendants, and then performed a perfect circumambulation of Śrīnivāsa.

The goddess danced before Supratīka, casting aside her shame and crying out, "Victory! O God! And at the time of the dance, having beheld the face of Hari with her gaze, she danced even more intensely.
O Śrīnivāsa, today my body has been purified; O Śrīnivāsa, today my eyes have become fruitful; and today my feet have truly become meaningful, O Lord Śrīnivāseśa, by performing this circumambulation.
"And today my two hands have become meaningful, having placed the name of Murāri at their forefront. Speaking thus and gladdening the God, she proceeded with a multitude of words of praise.
Then the gods' drums resounded and they rained down a shower of flowers upon his head; at that time, the celestial courtesans performed a dance on both sides of him.
In that very manner, O Lord of Sages, they all then made a sound like the clapping of palms and performed prostrations; on Mount Ānanda, she always causes them to dance in this way at all times.

Immersed in bliss, that goddess also went to her own hermitage together with Jaigīṣavya. O Lord of Sages, the noble ones say that for those who do not perform this pilgrimage in this manner, everything is fruitless.

Having gone to the hermitage together with Jaigīṣavya, he asked his guru for the mantra of Veṅkaṭeśa: "O Jaigīṣavya, tell me the meaning of the mantra, so that it may indeed bear fruit for those who perform its recitation."
Jaigīṣavya said: Listen, O blessed lady, to the meaning of the name Veṅkaṭeśa; having heard it, keep it firmly in your heart.
The syllable *vi* signifies the supreme; *ya* is declared to be knowledge (*jñāna*). The letter *ka* signifies bliss (*sukha*); *ṭa* is declared to be the mind (*citta*).
O maiden, it should be understood that the word "Īśa" refers to the Self; "jñeya" (the knowable) is perfect knowledge and bliss, and because of its all-pervasiveness, it is designated as "Vyaṅkaṭa."
Since the senses and so forth are said to be subordinate members (*vyaṅga*) in Hari, the prefix *vi-* signifies a collection;
thus, *vyaṅkaṭa* refers to the multitude of the senses.
Because he impels [the soul] toward himself, he is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa; because he constantly sends [the soul] toward the object [of experience], he is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa.
Because they consist of distinguished knowledge, the liberated ones are eternally remembered as *vyeti*; and the collection of the liberated ones is proclaimed as *Vyaṅkaṭa*.

Because he is the Lord of the multitude of those eternally liberated, he is named Vyaṅkaṭa; therefore, the individual soul (jīva), which consists of the subtle body (liṅgadeha), is designated as Vyaṅkaṭa.

Because he is the Lord of the *liṅgas*, he is designated as Vyaṅkaṭeśa; and because the hosts of Daityas are devoid of knowledge and other virtues, the multitude of Daityas is therefore proclaimed as Vyaṅkaṭa.
He who is the lord over their withdrawal is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa; for qualities such as desire and anger are opposed to bliss.
They were called the Vyaṅkaṭas; the Lord is their destroyer. Therefore, knowing him by the name Vyaṅkaṭeśa, perform your recitation.

O Lord of Birds, having thus heard the majesty of Vyaṅkaṭa, the goddess slept right there that night together with her father; then, rising at the Brāhma-muhūrta, the maiden remembered [it] in her heart.
(The Morning Praise of Vyaṅkaṭeśa): May Śrī Vyaṅkaṭeśa in the form of Nṛsiṃha, Śrī Varadarāja in the form of Varāha, Śrī Raṅgaśāyin, and Anantaśāyin—may they all grant me a beautiful dawn.
May Śrīkṛṣṇamūrti, Gadādhara, Śrīviṣṇupāda who dwells at Prayāga, and Nārāyaṇa who resides at Śrī Badarī—all of them grant me a beautiful dawn.
Dāmodara, indeed the abode of the three worlds, Śrī Pāṇḍuraṅga, Nṛsiṃhadeva, Śrī Rāmadeva, and Amoghavāsa—[these are] the destroyers of false views.
May Śrī Dharmaputra, Nṛsiṃhamūrti, Śrī Pippalastha, Muhallavāsa, Kolānṛsiṃha, and Siṃha residing at Śūrpakāra, grant their vision.
May the four-faced Brahmā, the beautiful Sarasvatī, our own mother Bhāratī, Śiva, Garuḍa, and Śeṣa, as well as Indra and the others headed by Śacī, grant us vision.
May Dvārāvatī, Kāśikā, Avantikā, Prayāga, Kāñcī, the city of Mathurā, Māyāvatī, and the city of Hastimatī all grant him their favor.
The Bhāgīrathī, the Sarasvatī, the Godāvarī, the Sindhu, the Kṛṣṇaveṇī, the Yamunā—daughter of Kalinda—and the Narmadā all flow there.
The Vitastā, Kāverī, Tuṅgabhadrā, Suvannarā, Bhīmarathī, Vipāśā, Sutāmraparṇī, Pinākinī, and Kruddhā;
Svāmipuṣkariṇī, as well as Suvarṇamukharī, Śrīpāṇḍavī, Taubaru, and Kapilā, which destroys all sins.
May the preceptor Vasiṣṭha, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Manu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Gautama, Raibhya, Marīci, Cyavana, and Dakṣa—may they all grant me a most auspicious dawn.
May the seven oceans, the seven great mountain ranges, the seven continents, the seven groves, and the seven worlds beginning with Bhūr, all together grant him prosperity.

May Māndhātṛ, Nahuṣa, Ambarīṣa, Sagara, King Nala, Dharmarāja, Prahlāda, Kratu-rāṭ, Vibhīṣaṇa, Gaya, Vyāsa, Hanūmān, Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, Umā, the daughter of Drupada, the illustrious Jānakī, Tārakā, Mandodarī, and all others, O Hari, constantly bring about a great dawn for me.

O Lord Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, may those forests of Aśvattha trees, as well as the groves of Tulasī and Dhātrī, O Master, the forests of Punnāga and Caṃpaka, other flowering plants, the groves of Mandāra, and even the Saugandhika flowers of Hari—may they all grant me eternal joy!

Having thus recollected Śrīnivāsa and performed her purification rites together with Jaigīṣavya, the goddess went to the lotus pond of Hari and bathed properly in that place. Having correctly recited the mantra of Vyaṅkaṭeśa, she spoke to Jaigīṣavya and her preceptor.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Goddess’s Vision and Praise of Veṅkaṭeśa," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

The Virgin said: "Tell me, for what purpose has Śrīnivāsa come here? Where was Śeṣācala, and when did he arrive, the destroyer of sins? And tell me, for what reason has Svāmipuṣkariṇī also come here?"
Jaigīṣavya said: Listen, O blessed and highly fortunate lady, to the arrival of Vyaṅkaṭeśa; O Goddess, O beautiful woman, our sins shall pass away like a difficult burden.
In ancient times, there was Hiraṇyākṣa, the son of Kaśyapa and Diti, who served as the guardian of the second door due to the verbal punishment inflicted by Sanaka and the others.
Born from the womb of a Daitya, he became a powerful thorn in the side of the gods; known as Saṃjīva and Vijaya, he was a great lord and a devotee of Hari.
Hiraṇyākṣa, the Daitya with eyes like a doe's, who personally reviled the devotees of Hari—such as he was, prepared himself to perform penance.

Then the goddess Diti, his mother, spoke to Hiraṇyākṣa. Diti said: "O illustrious one, you have been affectionate toward me since you were a mere calf, even when you were only eight years old while practicing austerities."
"Do not give me grief; this wise one will protect me. I cannot live for even a moment without you, for there is no life without you."
"Do not grieve, O illustrious one, for the sake of my life. Thus addressed by his mother, Vijaya, being under her influence, spoke as follows.

Hiraṇyākṣa said to his mother: "Abandoning this net, devote yourself fully to the service of Viṣṇu; withdraw your affection for me, which has grown deep out of concern for your son, both for the sake of happiness and sorrow in this world and the next."
O Mother, as long as you maintain affection for me, so long will you undergo perpetual suffering. O Mother, your notion of me as your son exists, and my notion of you as my mother likewise exists.
I have the notion of "father" toward my venerable father, but my notion of "husband" toward you is indeed false; for Hari alone creates everything, and that Murāri is certainly its perfect protector.
Therefore, Hari alone is truly the mother at all times; the motherhood of others is merely figurative. If motherhood were primary in you, tell me, who would be the mother of Droṇa and the rest?

If motherhood truly resided primarily in you, tell me, who would be the mother of Dhātṛ and the other gods? Since the world always proceeds from him, Hari—the ancient, unborn Viṣṇu—is forever the father.

If the father were always the primary protector, tell me, who would protect the child while still in the womb? If the protection of parents were the only rule, tell me, who would be the protectors of tortoises and other such creatures?

If parents possess the quality of protectors, tell me, who are the protectors of compassion and the other virtues? Since one takes on a body from the hell named Put, therefore the ancient Viṣṇu is the true protector of his sons.

O fair-browed one, neither I, nor the husband, nor the father and others, nor the mother, nor the younger siblings and so forth can save one from hell; Viṣṇu alone is the protector of all everywhere, and no other.

Having severed my illusion with the weapon of knowledge, you should practice the remembrance of Hari with devotion; for that remembrance of Viṣṇu, which is preceded by devotion, O Mother, removes all sins in every way.

Whoever performs the remembrance of Viṣṇu with devotion shall become a destroyer of sins. This body is difficult to obtain in the land of action; even there, it is rare to find devotion to the form of Viṣṇu in its midst.
"Your life has passed in vain; quickly take refuge at the feet of Śrīnivāsa. Having thus instructed his mother, that best of sons became an ascetic due to the influence of the Daitya.

Having indeed pleased the Four-faced One with devotion, that great-souled one obtained invincibility; then, having encircled the earth with his hand, that great-souled best of Daityas carried it away.

In the land of Śrīmuṣṭa, Hari appeared as the ancient Viṣṇu in the form of a boar; having split the ocean, that Great-Souled One entered it and [raised up] the earth situated in the netherworld (rasātala).

Having placed him upon the tip of his own tusk, he departed; and when he returned from that journey, the best of the Daityas arrived. Striking him at the root of the ear, he slew him and restored the earth as it was before.
Having established the elephants of the quarters, Viṣṇu, as Śrīvarāha, remained indeed at Śrīmuṣṭi; then Hari Viṣṇu reflected with devotion upon my human body today.

"Where will they worship me, or where shall I show them compassion? Having thought thus, Hari, the Lord of Beings, placed the immovable mountain known as Śeṣa upon the shoulders of Indra from the world of Vaikuṇṭha, and he himself descended to the surface of the earth.
Starting from the banks of the Suvarṇamukharī and extending as far as the Śrīkṛṣṇaveṇī, Garuḍadhvaja established that mountain.
At the tail of the mountain is Śrīśaila, while Ahobala is remembered as being in the middle; and the face of Śrīnivāsa is declared to be the sacred field (kṣetra).
In this Ahobala, that which is desired is accomplished through even slight austerity; for indeed, all the meritorious holy sites, such as the Gaṅgā and others, are truly present here.
Whoever constantly serves this [teaching], endowed with faith and devotion—the seeker of knowledge shall obtain knowledge, and the seeker of wealth shall obtain wealth.
One desiring a son obtains a son, and a king regains his kingdom; whatever a mortal desires, he attains it in every way.

Because that which is thought of is accomplished [there], they know it as Cintāmaṇi; and because of the abundance of lotus ponds and lakes on this mountain, those who know the true meaning call it Puṣkarādvī.
Because its nature is that of refined gold (śātakuṃbha), they know it as Kanakādri; and because it came from Vaikuṇṭha, it is remembered as Vaikuṇṭhādri.
Endowed with the sovereignty of nectar, he is remembered as Vyaṅkaṭādri; indeed, [this work contains] the full extent of the majesty of the mountain of Vyaṅkaṭeśa.

Even the four-faced Brahmā is not capable of describing fully those who practice supreme devotion day after day on Vyaṅkaṭādri; the lame would become swift-footed, and the sightless would possess lotus-like eyes.
The mute shall indeed become eloquent, the deaf shall become a listener; the barren woman shall have many sons, and the destitute shall become wealthy.
All this will certainly come to pass through mere devotion to the mountain; for who on earth truly knows the essential nature of Vyaṅkaṭādri?

For that man who knows the meritorious majesty of this mountain, having abandoned Māyāvī and the supreme bliss of the highest Vaikuṇṭha, rejoices together with Ramā on the banks of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī.
Salutations to you, Śrīnivāsa, the illustrious Lord of Vyaṅkaṭa, whose limbs are auspicious and wonderful, and who bestows desired objects upon his devotees.
O maiden, hear the majesty of Śrī Svāmipuṣkariṇī; Śrīnivāsa is ever present within the midst of Śvāmipuṣkariṇī.

For those who perform their ablutions there, liberation is held in the palm of their hand. Three crores and a half crores of sacred fords (*tīrtha*) in the three worlds—all of them are eternally present at that very sacred ford of Hari.
That sacred ford named Śrīnivāsa is saluted by all the gods; it alone is celebrated as the temple of Śrīnivāsa.
O daughters, by the mere sight of it, sins are reduced to ashes; by each single bath alone, association with the virtuous becomes certain.

Having attained knowledge through association with the virtuous, one finds liberation through that knowledge; this is indeed the case for those who are qualified, but the opposite is true for those who are not practitioners of yoga.
Those who believe that people attain liberation merely by bathing at sacred fords (tīrtha) should all be known as asuras; indeed, they go to the lowest state.
O two maidens, in this sacred ford of Śrīnivāsa, in the northwestern corner, Vāyu always resides in order to perform the unsurpassed worship of Viṣṇu.
That is declared to be Vāyutīrtha, situated at a distance of twelve cubits; it is said to measure six cubits on the west and six cubits on the north; thus Vāyutīrtha is described.

O fair daughter, may those who are indeed Vaiṣṇavas, the foremost among the servants of Viṣṇu, perform their ablutions there first; and may the compassionate Śrīnivāsa, who dwells within the honey, be eternally pleased with me through bathing here.

O Goddess, those who desire to bathe at Madhvatīrtha—the great ones such as Rudra and others who are devoted to Vāyu—always perform their ablutions there in the morning, even before the rising of the sun.
O maiden, those who discharge bodily impurities, urine, vomit, or phlegm at the Vāyu-tīrtha, and those who perform the cleansing of the anus or the genitals there, are indeed asuras and rākṣasas.
O Goddess, what can I describe of the merit of those who listen to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa? O Goddess, [what of] those who mutter the Kṛṣṇa-mantra, that most secret and excellent eight-syllabled mantra?

Hari, Keśava, is exceedingly pleased with them; he dwells within the honey—of this there is no doubt. Thus do those who indeed give gifts to the foremost of the twice-born, to the Vaiṣṇavas, and to the learned.
The gods do not know their merit at all; only Śrīnivāsa, Hari, knows it. He who gives a Śālagrāma at Vāyutīrtha—Śrī Vyaṅkaṭeśa alone knows their merit.

O Goddess, bathing at Vāyutīrtha with a desireless mind is very difficult even for Vaiṣṇavas to attain; yet, by the power of fortune, even at that sacred site, the hearing of the Bhāgavata from the servants of Viṣṇu is obtained.

Likewise, O Goddess, at that sacred ford (tīrtha), it is difficult to find a gift of a Śālagrāma stone to an excellent brahmin—one that has the shape of a jambu fruit, is of a beautiful dark-blue color, possesses two faces, and is endowed with four discs.

The great ones declare that the Jānārdanī image is endowed with beautiful filaments, a banner marked with gold, and *kuśa* grass and barley marked with vajras; a gift to her at that sacred ford is difficult to obtain.

O auspicious lady, the gift of an image is most excellent, supreme, and very difficult to obtain; there should be no greed in this matter. Likewise, the gift of a cow that has calved once and yields much milk, as well as gifts of garments, jewels, and so forth, is very difficult to attain.

O Goddess, the great ones say that the gift of material wealth is the most excellent, and that the gift of what one desires for oneself is likewise great; however, they say that the gift of clothing which yields no fruit for oneself is useless.

The merit of giving a first-calf cow in milk is not attained by cows that have already been milked; likewise, for people, it is exceedingly difficult to possess the supreme wisdom required for the most excellent gift of clothing.

O daughter, the book of the Bhāgavata is most excellent and very difficult to obtain; and Vāyutīrtha, O Goddess, is likewise most excellent and very difficult for men to reach. Indeed, O daughter, reflection upon Hari by Vaiṣṇavas who know the truth is very rare, as is [the attainment of] Vāyutīrtha.
Situated to the north of the Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha is that which is called Candratīrtha; there the Moon always resides.
Remaining there, he performs the worship of Śrīnivāsa; and in that meritorious place, O two maidens, they perform their ablutions.
They are liberated from sins such as violating the teacher's bed; of this there is no doubt. Having bathed there, he who offers a śālagrāma stone on the eastern side [attains the same].
One attains liberation through knowledge; there is no need for further deliberation on this point. Furthermore, the gift of the Dadhivāmana image is exceedingly difficult to obtain there.
O auspicious maiden, it should be the size of a jujube fruit, round, blue in color, with a serene face, subtle, and very smooth.
It is equipped with two wheels, joined with five bull-riders, provided with a bow and arrows, and has the form of an endless coil.
Adorned with a forest garland, endowed with bliss, and possessing a thousand heads; joined with silver dots, it has the measure of half a *bhadrā* on the right side.

O Goddess, that which is accompanied by Candra is called Dadhivāmana; such a form, O beautiful lady, is difficult for men to attain in the Kali age and bestows great fortune. Know that image, O fair one, to be equal to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa.

The gift of that form is very difficult to obtain, and its hearing at Candratīrtha is hard to accomplish; indeed, hearing the true nature of Dadhivāmana from a Vaiṣṇava is exceedingly difficult to achieve.
Having bathed there and heard the account of Vāmana’s true form, they know that the fruit of their gift is equal [to other great gifts]. The Candratīrtha is declared to be ten cubits in measurement.
At midday, bathing is difficult for men to obtain there at that most auspicious place; staying there, the fortunate man always worships Hari.
The gift of a Śālagrāma in the form of a boar is indeed rare; it should be the size of a rose-apple fruit or like a hen's egg.
The face is ring-shaped, and its size is like that of a chickpea or similar; it is located on the left side of the deity, avoiding the middle region.
O beautiful lady, that which is joined with two wheels at the region of the head and endowed with a golden drop is called Bhūvarāha.

Having performed worship of Bhūvarāha, having given gifts to the distressed, and having listened to the sacred recitation, and having beheld Bhūvarāha stationed there—that man indeed has accomplished his purpose in this world.

Having bathed there, O Goddess, whoever correctly hears the characteristics of Bhūvarāha, the Mortal, attains merit through that; he becomes a partaker of liberation—there is no doubt to be made here.
O Goddess, in the northeast corner of Śrīnivāsa is the supreme purifying holy site (tīrtha) of Rudra; staying there, the high-souled Lord Rudra performs worship of Śrīnivāsa eternally.

They say its measurement is eight cubits; indeed, a bath there must be performed by the Vaiṣṇavas. Having bathed there, being self-restrained, one should listen with devotion to the divine story of Murāri. One should perform bathing, drinking, and giving of gifts there; O Goddess, Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha is eternally pleased [by this]. (3.26.76)
And it is the size of a jujube fruit, circular, and joined with a dot.
On the left side of the deity, however, there should be two wheels, joined with golden lines and slightly tinged with red.
Know that Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, whose complexion is like that of a Vaiśya, whose face is adorned with marks such as lotus lines, is the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

O Lord of Sages, know that such a gift of a stone slab from a quarry for the sake of an image is difficult to accomplish; having bathed there, one should listen with devotion to the form of Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the Lord of Lakṣmī.
O Goddess, one obtains the fruit from the gift of an image; this is the truth, the truth—there is no need for deliberation here.
Between Īśāna and Śakra, the Brahma-tīrtha is proclaimed; bathing there is difficult for humans to attain, yet it accomplishes all goals.
Indeed, the gift of a Śālagrāma stone is difficult for men to obtain there; the gift of the very form of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is exceedingly rare.
The ground should be equal to an udumbara fruit; that is declared to be the proper measure. It should be shaped like an umbrella, circular, with a serene appearance, and auspicious.
The mouth is said to be the size of a chickpea region, provided with abundant [teeth] on both the left and right sides.
It was the color of a calf from a herd of cows, equipped with four wheels, joined with cow-hooves, and marked with golden calluses.
Adorned with a forest garland and equipped with arrow-fletchings made of vajra—such a form as this, they know, is Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
In the Kali age, O Goddess, its attainment by men on earth is remembered as difficult to achieve; giving a gift is even more difficult—what more shall I tell you?
Having bathed at the Brahmatīrtha, one should indeed listen to the narrations of Hari, as well as those concerning Gaṇḍikā, Śilā, and Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
Whoever understands the characteristic [of an action] will certainly obtain a result corresponding to it; of this there is no doubt, and no deliberation is required in this matter.
To the east of the Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha lies Indratīrtha; there the Lord of Śacī resides in order to perform the worship of Śrīnivāsa.
The gift of a Śālagrāma stone should indeed be made to a learned Brāhmaṇa; the gift of a Śālagrāma stone destroys ten million killings.
O Goddess, O auspicious one, he who bestows upon the earth at that sacred ford a stone known as Sītārāmaśilā shall become equal to a king.
O Goddess, the Sītārāma stone is proclaimed to be of two kinds: one endowed with five wheels, and another joined with six wheels.
Among those as well, the one endowed with six wheels is proclaimed as the most excellent; and the fruit of that which is endowed with five wheels is said to be twofold.
It is the size of a hen’s egg, very smooth, and blue in color; it is endowed with three faces and possesses six wheels and filaments.
O auspicious lady, that which is joined with a golden line and endowed with a banner, a vajra, and a goad is indeed known by the name Sītārāma.
O Goddess, this treasury of Sītā and Rāma’s words regarding salutation and non-salutation is auspicious and bestows its own sovereignty; it is indeed difficult for men to obtain in the Kali age.
O Great Goddess, at Indratīrtha there is the stone known as Sītārāma; the gift bestowed there is difficult to attain, and it is not the fruit of meager austerity.
But if one lacks the capacity for giving, one should listen to the characteristics of Hari; one shall obtain that same fruit which is gained from the gift of a Śālagrāma stone.

O Goddess, in the south-eastern corner there exists the highly praised sacred ford (tīrtha) of Śrīnivāsa known as Vahni; that god Vahni indeed always remains within the midst of that ford to perform the worship of Śrīnivāsa.

O Goddess, whoever performs a bath with devotion at the sacred ford known as Vahni while remembering the Unborn (Aja), attains liberation through the gateway of knowledge; O Goddess, such a bath there is indeed difficult for men to obtain.

O Goddess, knowing that bathing at the king of holy places is difficult to perform and that devotion toward it is likewise hard to attain, the gift of a Śālagrāma stone—specifically one named Vāsudeva—is even more exceedingly rare.

Short, circular, blue in color, subtle, with a pure face and a perfect mouth-circle, joined with an excellent bamboo—O auspicious lady, such a gift called Vāsudeva is difficult to obtain in the Kali age.

O Goddess, if one lacks the capacity for that gift, then having bathed in the holy ford named Vāsudeva, the characteristics of the stone should be properly recited; the great ones say the fruit of these two is equal.
To the south of Śrīnivāsa, Yamatīrtha is remembered; there resides King Yama himself, always performing worship of Hari.
In that place, bathing and giving gifts are remembered as supremely inexhaustible; O great sage, the gift of a Śālagrāma stone should be performed there.
The offering of a stone known as *paṭṭābhirāma* is desired; it is as large as a mango fruit and is endowed with three faces.
Deprived of its head by the discus, yet endowed with seven discs, it was blue in color, marked with golden lines, and possessed of a cow-horn and other such features.

The Paṭṭavardhana Rāma is indeed difficult to obtain and bestows great fortune; whoever offers the Paṭṭavardhana Rāma there, he shall indeed be consecrated with the royal turban—of this there is no doubt.
To the southwest of Śrīnivāsa is the excellent Nairṛta Tīrtha; for Nirṛti always resides there in order to perform worship.
There, one should perform a ritual bath; then rebirth no longer exists. [This applies] to the stone known as Puruṣottama belonging to the Śālagrāma rock.
That mortal who provides an image—shaped like an udumbara fruit, with a serene face and auspicious—attains the supreme goal.
It is joined with two wheels, endowed with a wheel at the head, marked with a golden drop, and provided with a vajra-hook.

The gift of that image is difficult to obtain, for it is therein that the high-souled Lord Śrīnivāsa is pleased; O Goddess, when such a gift is difficult to accomplish, then the characteristics of that image must be heard.
Between the Pāśī and Nairṛta [tīrthas], the supreme Śeṣa-tīrtha is remembered; having bathed there, one should present an image of Śeṣa to a twice-born man.
He goes to the supreme world, from which there is no return; it is shaped like the fruit of the udumbara tree and is also spiral in form.
His speech is like that of the remainder; in him, two wheels are traditionally taught. His fruit is joined with a single wheel and accompanied by an anthill.
Endowed with some degree of color and clearly manifest to the intellect, the form of Śeṣa is declared to be twofold: asleep and awakened.
The awakened [serpent] has its hood raised and is endowed with seven hundred thousand hoods; even among those, the sleeping one is rare and is remembered as the bestower of great fortune.
It bestows liberation both in this world and in the next; of this there is no doubt. It begins from the nine wheels and extends up to the twenty, wherever it may be.
He should indeed be known as Ananta, for he bestows infinite fruit; O fair-faced one, he should be known as Viśvambhara beyond twenty [fingers].
Even there, it is endowed with filaments and the single characteristic; however, in the Kali age, it is difficult for men to obtain, and the gift of it is exceedingly rare.
Having bathed in the Śeṣatīrtha with a perfectly pure mind and having heard the description of these [shrines], one attains the supreme goal.
Beyond that, O highly fortunate lady, is the supreme Vāruṇa Tīrtha; there dwells the god Varuṇa, always performing worship of Hari.

There, one should perform a ritual bath and bestow the highest gift; O lady of excellent complexion, one who desires prosperity should give a crocodile, a fish, or even a *trivikrama* at this sacred ford.
It has the shape of a jambu fruit; it is fine at the tail and marked with spots; there are three wheels on its face, and it has a wheel upon its tail.
The form of Matsya is described as being enriched with the Śrīvatsa mark and rows of dots; the Śiśumāra is described as having a discus below its tail.
If it is joined with a curved disc, it is declared to be Trivikrama; having heard the characteristics of these [images] at the supreme sacred ford of Vāruṇa.

Having obtained the fruit of this gift, one rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu. O beautiful lady, in whichever house the aforementioned forms reside, the Bhāgīrathī, the best of sacred fords, dwells there; of this there is no doubt.
O Lord, bathing in the Puṣkariṇī is difficult for men in the Kali age; indeed, bathing even in the sacred sites situated there is exceedingly difficult.
The gift of a Śālagrāma stone is likewise remembered as difficult to accomplish; on the bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the gift of a daughter in marriage is exceedingly difficult to achieve.
The gift of a Kapila cow is difficult to accomplish, and the gift of edible food is even more difficult to accomplish at the Svāmipuṣkariṇī Tīrtha or at other sacred fords, O beautiful lady.
"Perform your bath according to the rule, and likewise perform the gift of a bed. Thus was the maiden addressed by the sage Jaigīṣavya.
Firm in her vows, she performed her bath at Svāmipuṣkariṇī; having bathed well in these sacred fords, the beautiful woman made offerings.
She dwelt there for twenty-one days; whoever hears of the greatness of the banks of Svāmipuṣkariṇī attains supreme devotion toward Śrīnivāsa, who pervades the universe.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Vyaṅkaṭagiri, the Sacred Tirthas such as Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the Deities Residing Therein, the Characteristics of Their Śālagrāmas, and the Gift of Them," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
(Śrīgaruḍa Mahāpurāṇa— 27)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Then, desiring to bathe, she went to the Nandā river which wards off sin; there, the wise woman, bowing low with humility, questioned that brahmin preceptor.
"O Brahmin, what is the name of this river, and what is my duty here? Tell me. Thus addressed, Jaigīṣavya spoke these words.
Jaigīṣavya said: Listen, O blessed lady, I shall proclaim this greatness that destroys sin; O highly fortunate one, this river is always a destroyer of evil.
The flood of sins such as the killing of a Brahmin is destroyed by bathing here; indeed, this is seen directly by those who have prepared to perform their ablutions.
And water is perceived as impure due to sins; O Goddess, one should perform the ritual bath only so long as the water appears pure.
As long as pure water has not arrived, so long does sin not perish; once pure water has arrived, it is certain that sin is destroyed.

O large-eyed one, such is the greatness of Kalāvi seen upon this earth. Here, one should perform ablutions and bestow the highest gifts; then, having attained knowledge, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
From approaching the wife of his guru, Candra [fell]; Hari went [to hell] for violating Ahalyā; Śukra for drinking liquor; and Bali for stealing gold.
O beautiful lady, Rudra was liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin, the Naga from stealing what was given, and Rāma from the murder of a Sūta—all were indeed freed here.
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a sacred ford equal to this; perform your ablutions here, O illustrious lady, for by this you shall indeed attain perfection.
Together with her father, the sage Jaigīṣavya, the beautiful maiden performed her ablutions according to the prescribed rites and then arose.
For as long as the *pauruṣa-sūkta* lasts, it indeed remains; thereafter, one should recite the supreme great mantra known by the name Veṅkaṭeśa.
Having gratified the twice-born with garments, wealth, ornaments, and other gifts, the goddess departed from there for the supreme Kamārī-tīrtha.
Having heard of the greatness of Kumārī, that goddess performed her ablutions; then, returning once more, she indeed reached the Virajā river along the way.
Having seen him, that goddess questioned her lord and teacher Jaigīṣavya: "O best of Brahmins, who is this woman? Tell me, what is the purpose here?"
Thus questioned, Jaigīṣavya, that ocean of compassion, spoke: "O daughter of Bhagīratha, here indeed comes [the river] through this very path."
Therefore, she is indeed called the "Internal Gaṅgā" by the supreme sages; O maiden, her water is always dear to the abode of Śrī.
Whoever performs a bath here attains the supreme goal; that maiden performed her bath in the supremely purifying water.
Having thus understood the nature of charity and the other virtues, she recited the supreme mantra; then the beautiful woman returned once more to the presence of Śrīnivāsa.
Having gratified the Brahmins and others with garments, perfumes, ornaments, and other gifts, he performed a circumambulation limb by limb of Veṅkaṭanāyaka with devotion.
Again, on the following morning, having bathed in the waters of Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the illustrious lady went to the place known as Tuṃburu.

The Goddess asked that Guru, her Lord: "What is the name of this woman? Jaigīṣavya said: "This woman of excellent complexion is indeed one who possesses the supernatural knowledge (abhijñā) of Tuṃburu."
Formerly, while Nārada was established in ascetic penance together with Tumburu, Viṣṇu appeared here for the benefit of Nārada.
Indeed, he who performs a bath here attains the supreme goal; for all human beings, bathing here is difficult to obtain in the Kali age.
For humans, bathing here is not the fruit of minor austerity; having bathed there, drunk [the water], and given gifts, one becomes free from hair.
Having returned, that goddess bowed down to Śrīnivāsa; on that day, O beautiful lady, she gratified the Brahmins with offerings.
Having reached Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the virtuous and highly fortunate lady lit lamps upon the steps; with those rows of lamps, she swiftly gratified the Lord of Gods, Śrīnivāsa, the Teacher of the World.
When the following day arrived, that most excellent Śakratīrtha—known as Kapila—is remembered as a purifying sacred site located in the upper region.
Having bathed there, O highly fortunate one, she herself should subsequently bathe him; there is the Viṣvasena lake, which destroys all sins.
Thereafter, the illustrious lady went there and beheld the sacred bathing places of the five weapons; she performed her ablutions in them.

Above that, there should be a fire-pit (agnikuṇḍa) which is difficult to ascend; and in front of that, upon it, is the Brahma-tīrtha, which grants liberation from the sin of killing a Brahmin (brahmahatyā).

Above that, however, is the meritorious sacred site (tīrtha) of the Seven Sages (Saptarṣis), which yields excellent fruit; for each of those sacred sites, the fruit increases tenfold as one proceeds further upward.
And who indeed here is worthy to describe the majesty of these? That maiden performed supreme austerity at the sacred fords of the seers.
Having performed supreme austerity until my descent, and having abandoned the body through the practice of yoga, you shall be born in the house of Jāmbavān.
Born by the name Jāmbavatī, she grew up in his household. Her father, Jāmbavān, then gave that maiden to him; O Lord of Birds, this very Rukmiṇī was my wife.
For who else on earth besides me is able to describe this supreme narrative of the great mountain Veṅkaṭādri?
Lakṣmī indeed always prepares the food offering for Veṅkaṭeśa, and Brahmā worships him constantly; such is the conclusion of the scriptures.

One should not mock men who consume the food offerings (naivedya); however, if one lacks the capacity to partake of it oneself, then items such as jaggery and the like may certainly be accepted from the offerings—of this there is no doubt; otherwise, one will become a denizen of hell.

There has never been, nor will there ever be, a deity superior to Śrīnivāsa. Having yourself cooked food such as that prepared with ghee, you should partake of a meal only after offering it as *naivedya* to Śrīnivāsa.

This which has been told to you, O Lord of Birds, is supremely secret; it must not be spoken to anyone because of its secrecy, O best of birds. Hereafter, I shall explain the gradations [of excellence]; listen, O Lord.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, titled "Description of the Various Pilgrimages Undertaken by Brahmā and Kanyā," in the glorious *Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa*.
In a previous creation, she who was Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Rudra, having cast off her body at Dakṣa’s sacrifice, was born from Menakā on Mount Hemavān, the sustainer of the earth.

O Lord of Birds, she who was formerly Pārvatī, the wife of Rudra, and Vāruṇī, the wife of Śeṣa—that very same woman of great devotion to her husband has now arrived with Balabhadra to sport, having assumed a dual form.
The one named Śrī is endowed with the presence of Indirā; her second image is in the form of a cloud. Indeed, when Viṣṇu performed penance together with Vīndra, she was present in the form of Śeṣa.
At that very time, the goddess Vāruṇī, the wife of Śeṣa, performed penance for the sake of pleasing Indirā. Then Indirā, being pleased and well-disposed, spoke to Vāruṇī, the wife of Śeṣa.

O blessed one, when Rāma, endowed with a portion of Viṣṇu, shall appear upon the earth as the son of Rohiṇī, you too, united with me through my entry into you, shall be known as Śrī to sport with Balabhadra.

"You shall attain [perfection]; there is no need for further deliberation on this," she said, and having spoken, she indeed departed for the world of Viṣṇu. Having received the praiseworthy name "Śrī" in the world from a portion of Śrī Lakṣmī, she became the wife of Śeṣa.

When Īśa uplifts the vast [earth], then Rāma, at the confluence of Śrī and Bhidā, always brings about the satisfaction of Ramā; indeed, her very manifestation (āveśa) is the union that destroys the darkness of the three qualities.

She who is Revatī, the daughter of Raivata, is Vāruṇī, the wife of Balabhadra. O King of Birds, know that those three wives of Bala named after Suparṇā are twice as inferior to the wives of Viṣṇu; and you, my grandson, should understand that you are ten times more inferior than Rudra, Śeṣa, and the others.
